archetypes.fit-estimate: fit a model to data and estimate its parameters (with uncertainties where natural)
archetypes.predict: build a predictive model from training data and predict held-out targets
archetypes.classify-detect: classify, detect, identify or flag items, events, signals or anomalies in data
archetypes.reconstruct-invert: reconstruct a hidden quantity, state, signal or structure from indirect or degraded measurements
archetypes.simulate-compute: implement a numerical model, simulation or solver and compute requested quantities
archetypes.design-optimize: design, tune or control a system, or solve an optimization problem, to meet stated targets
archetypes.process-pipeline: build a processing or reduction pipeline that turns raw data into specified derived products
archetypes.infer-test: statistical or causal inference: test hypotheses, estimate effects, quantify evidence
archetypes.prove-derive: prove, formally verify or exactly derive a mathematical result

modalities.tabular: tables of measurements or records (CSV, Parquet, Excel)
modalities.time-series: time series or signals (sensor traces, recordings, light curves, logs over time)
modalities.image: images, image stacks or video (microscopy, astronomy, medical, remote sensing)
modalities.sequence: biological or symbolic sequences (DNA, RNA, protein, reads, alignments)
modalities.structure: molecular, crystal or 3-D structures and meshes (PDB, CIF, XYZ, STL)
modalities.gridded-field: gridded or spatial fields (NetCDF, HDF5 arrays, rasters, spatial point data)
modalities.graph: graphs and networks (adjacency lists, interaction networks, road or power grids)
modalities.spectrum: spectra (optical, mass, NMR, X-ray, frequency-domain measurements)
modalities.model-spec: a model, system or problem specification without a dataset (equations, netlists, parameter files, formal statements, instance files)

field_desc.physics: physics (classical and quantum mechanics, optics, plasma, condensed matter, nuclear and particle, acoustics, fluids, statistical physics)
field_desc.chemistry: chemistry (physical, analytical, organic, inorganic, computational and quantum chemistry, spectroscopy, kinetics, electrochemistry)
field_desc.materials-science: materials science (crystallography, microstructure, mechanical and electronic properties, polymers, alloys, batteries and energy materials, characterization)
field_desc.astronomy: astronomy and astrophysics (photometry, spectroscopy, astrometry, time-domain, cosmology, planetary science, instrumentation)
field_desc.biology: biology (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, structural biology, evolution, cell and molecular biology, microbiology, systems biology, bioinformatics)
field_desc.medicine: medicine and health sciences (clinical data, epidemiology, medical imaging, physiology signals, pharmacology, biostatistics of trials)
field_desc.neuroscience: neuroscience (electrophysiology, spike trains, neuroimaging, behaviour, neural models)
field_desc.ecology: ecology and environmental biology (populations, communities, biodiversity surveys, movement, species distributions)
field_desc.mechanical-engineering: mechanical and aerospace engineering (dynamics, control, vibration, structures, thermal and fluid systems, robotics, manufacturing)
field_desc.electrical-engineering: electrical and electronic engineering (circuits, signal processing, communications, power systems, control, embedded and RF)
field_desc.civil-engineering: civil and environmental engineering (structures, geotechnics, hydraulics and hydrology, transportation, construction materials)
field_desc.statistics: statistics and data science (inference, regression, Bayesian methods, time series, survival, experimental design, causal inference)
field_desc.operations-research: operations research (optimization, scheduling, routing, queueing, inventory, stochastic programming, network flows)
field_desc.applied-mathematics: applied mathematics (numerical analysis, ODE/PDE, dynamical systems, inverse problems, approximation, signal and harmonic analysis)
field_desc.formal-mathematics: formal and computational mathematics (machine-checked proofs, combinatorics, number theory and algebra computations, verified algorithms)
field_desc.geosciences: geosciences (seismology, geophysics, geochemistry, hydrogeology, remote sensing of land, atmosphere and climate, geodesy)
field_desc.ocean-sciences: ocean sciences (physical oceanography, ocean biogeochemistry, waves and tides, marine acoustics, ocean observing systems)

physics.name: Multibody and rigid-body dynamics simulation
physics.gist: Model linked rigid bodies, gyroscopes or mechanisms with constraints, integrate the equations of motion with structure-preserving or DAE solvers, and extract trajectories, reaction forces or conserved-quantity drift.

physics.name: Orbital mechanics and perturbation analysis
physics.gist: Propagate satellite or planetary orbits under J2, drag, third-body or radiation-pressure perturbations, fit orbital elements to tracking data, and compute transfers or resonances.

physics.name: Nonlinear oscillators and chaos diagnostics
physics.gist: Simulate or analyse driven, coupled or delayed nonlinear oscillators, computing bifurcation diagrams, Poincaré sections, Lyapunov exponents and basins from simulations or measured time series.

physics.name: Structural vibration and experimental modal analysis
physics.gist: Estimate natural frequencies, damping ratios and mode shapes from accelerometer or hammer-test data, or from beam and plate models, and update the models to match measurements.

physics.name: Granular media and discrete element modelling
physics.gist: Simulate assemblies of frictional grains with soft-contact DEM to study packing, flow, jamming, hopper discharge or force chains, and compare with continuum rheology laws.

physics.name: Finite element continuum elasticity
physics.gist: Solve linear or hyperelastic boundary-value problems on meshed geometries to obtain stress, strain and buckling loads, including convergence checks and comparison with analytic limits.

physics.name: Time-dependent Schrödinger wavepacket propagation
physics.gist: Propagate wavepackets in 1D to 3D potentials with split-operator or Crank-Nicolson schemes to compute tunnelling rates, transmission spectra, revivals or autocorrelation functions.

physics.name: Open quantum systems and master equations
physics.gist: Model dissipation and decoherence with Lindblad or Redfield equations or quantum trajectories, computing steady states, emission spectra, correlation functions and relaxation rates.

physics.name: Quantum state and process tomography
physics.gist: Reconstruct density matrices or process maps from simulated or measured projective counts using maximum-likelihood, Bayesian or compressed-sensing estimators with error bars.

physics.name: Coherent control of few-level quantum systems
physics.gist: Model, design and analyse driven dynamics of few-level quantum systems. Covers Rabi and Ramsey sequences, adiabatic passage and Landau-Zener transitions, composite and robust pulses, dynamical decoupling filter functions, optimal-control pulse shaping, and gate-fidelity or leakage evaluation under drive constraints, detuning and noise.

physics.name: Quantum scattering and phase-shift analysis
physics.gist: Compute partial-wave phase shifts, cross sections, resonances and scattering lengths for model or empirical potentials, or invert measured cross sections for potential parameters.

physics.name: Superconducting and trapped-ion qubit characterization
physics.gist: Fit Rabi, Ramsey, echo, T1/T2, randomized-benchmarking and readout-histogram data to extract qubit frequencies, coherence times, gate fidelities and assignment errors.

physics.name: Atomic level structure and spectral calculations
physics.gist: Compute energy levels, Zeeman and Stark shifts, hyperfine structure and transition strengths of atoms or ions from model Hamiltonians, and fit them to measured line positions.

physics.name: Gaussian beam and ray-transfer optical design
physics.gist: Use ABCD matrices and Gaussian beam propagation to design resonators, beam expanders, mode-matching optics or relay systems that meet waist, divergence and stability specifications.

physics.name: Thin-film multilayer coating design
physics.gist: Compute reflectance and transmittance spectra of dielectric or metal stacks with transfer matrices, and optimise layer thicknesses for filters, mirrors or anti-reflection coatings, or fit measured spectra.

physics.name: Fourier optics and diffraction simulation
physics.gist: Simulate Fresnel and Fraunhofer propagation, apertures, gratings, holograms and imaging point-spread and transfer functions using angular-spectrum and FFT methods.

physics.name: Phase retrieval and wavefront sensing
physics.gist: Recover optical phase from intensity measurements with Gerchberg-Saxton, ptychographic or Shack-Hartmann reconstruction, and decompose the resulting wavefronts into Zernike aberrations.

physics.name: Nonlinear pulse propagation in optical fibers
physics.gist: Solve the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation with split-step methods to model dispersion, self-phase modulation, solitons and supercontinuum, or to fit fiber parameters from measured spectra.

physics.name: Photonic waveguide and resonator mode solving
physics.gist: Compute guided modes, effective indices, dispersion, bend losses and coupling for slab, rib, fiber or ring-resonator geometries with finite-difference or semi-analytic solvers.

physics.name: Interferometric fringe analysis
physics.gist: Extract phase maps, surface profiles or displacements from interferograms and fringe sequences using phase-shifting, Fourier-transform and phase-unwrapping algorithms.

physics.name: Laser rate equations and cavity dynamics
physics.gist: Model gain media and cavities with rate equations to predict thresholds, relaxation oscillations, Q-switched and mode-locked pulses, and fit them to measured light-current or temporal data.

physics.name: Spectrometer calibration and line-profile fitting
physics.gist: Calibrate wavelength and instrument response of optical spectra and fit Voigt or more complex line profiles to extract positions, widths, broadening mechanisms and intensities.

physics.name: Langmuir probe and electrostatic plasma diagnostics
physics.gist: Analyse probe I-V characteristics, including sheath and magnetic effects, to infer electron temperature, density, plasma potential and electron energy distributions.

physics.name: Particle-in-cell plasma simulation
physics.gist: Run 1D or 2D electrostatic PIC codes to study two-stream and beam instabilities, Landau damping, sheaths or wave-particle interactions, with diagnostics such as growth rates and phase-space maps.

physics.name: MHD equilibrium and stability
physics.gist: Solve Grad-Shafranov or reduced MHD equations for magnetic confinement configurations and evaluate safety factor profiles, pressure limits and ideal or resistive instability growth.

physics.name: Charged-particle orbits in electromagnetic fields
physics.gist: Integrate full-orbit or guiding-center motion with Boris or symplectic pushers in magnetic mirrors, tokamaks, radiation belts or traps to study drifts, confinement and adiabatic invariants.

physics.name: Plasma wave dispersion relations
physics.gist: Numerically solve kinetic or fluid dispersion relations with plasma dispersion functions to obtain wave branches, damping and instability thresholds for given distributions.

physics.name: Space plasma in-situ data analysis
physics.gist: Process spacecraft magnetometer and particle data to identify shocks, current sheets and turbulence, perform minimum-variance and spectral analyses, and estimate plasma moments.

physics.name: Collisional-radiative plasma spectroscopy
physics.gist: Build collisional-radiative models of level populations and use line ratios and broadening to infer electron temperature and density from emission spectra of laboratory or astrophysical plasmas.

physics.name: Tight-binding band structure and topology
physics.gist: Construct tight-binding Hamiltonians for lattices, ribbons or heterostructures and compute bands, densities of states, Berry curvature, Chern or Z2 invariants and edge states.

physics.name: Powder diffraction indexing and structure refinement
physics.gist: Index X-ray or neutron powder patterns, fit peak profiles, refine lattice and structural parameters, and estimate crystallite size and strain from peak broadening.

physics.name: Lattice dynamics and phonon dispersion
physics.gist: Compute phonon dispersions, densities of states and thermal properties from force-constant models or empirical potentials, and fit force constants to measured dispersion data.

physics.name: Electrical and magnetotransport measurement analysis
physics.gist: Analyse resistivity, Hall, magnetoresistance and quantum-oscillation data to extract carrier densities, mobilities, effective masses, weak-localization parameters or superconducting transitions.

physics.name: Quantum spin models by exact diagonalization
physics.gist: Diagonalise Heisenberg, Hubbard or transverse-field Ising Hamiltonians on finite clusters using symmetries and Lanczos to obtain gaps, correlations, entanglement and dynamical structure factors.

physics.name: Classical molecular dynamics of materials
physics.gist: Run MD simulations with empirical interatomic potentials to compute elastic constants, diffusion coefficients, melting points, thermal conductivity or defect energetics.

physics.name: Magnetization, hysteresis and micromagnetics
physics.gist: Model hysteresis loops, domain walls and anisotropy with Stoner-Wohlfarth, Preisach or finite-difference micromagnetic simulations, and fit magnetometry data for material parameters.

physics.name: Semiconductor device drift-diffusion modelling
physics.gist: Solve the Poisson and drift-diffusion equations for diodes, transistors or solar cells to obtain band diagrams and I-V and C-V curves, and extract doping and lifetime parameters from measurements.

physics.name: Gamma-ray spectroscopy and activity determination
physics.gist: Calibrate HPGe or scintillator spectra, fit photopeaks over Compton backgrounds, identify nuclides and compute activities with efficiency, decay and coincidence corrections.

physics.name: Radioactive decay chains and activation analysis
physics.gist: Solve Bateman equations for decay and activation chains under irradiation histories to predict inventories and dose rates, or infer half-lives and branching ratios from count data.

physics.name: Neutron and photon transport Monte Carlo
physics.gist: Write Monte Carlo transport codes for slabs, spheres and shields to compute flux spectra, attenuation, buildup factors, dose and multiplication with variance reduction.

physics.name: Collider event kinematics and resonance fits
physics.gist: Reconstruct invariant masses and kinematic variables from event-level data, and fit signal-plus-background models to extract resonance masses, widths, yields and significances.

physics.name: Charged-particle track reconstruction
physics.gist: Reconstruct tracks and vertices from detector hits with pattern recognition, Kalman fitting and multiple-scattering models, and measure momentum resolution and efficiency.

physics.name: Calorimeter and detector energy calibration
physics.gist: Calibrate detector channel responses with test-beam, cosmic or source data, correct nonlinearity and leakage, and determine energy resolution parameters.

physics.name: Neutrino oscillation parameter inference
physics.gist: Compute oscillation probabilities including matter effects and fit event spectra from reactor, accelerator or atmospheric experiments to constrain mixing angles and mass splittings.

physics.name: Nuclear reactor kinetics and criticality
physics.gist: Solve point-kinetics and diffusion equations with delayed neutrons and feedback to study reactivity transients, criticality eigenvalues, flux shapes and control-rod worth.

physics.name: Room acoustics and reverberation analysis
physics.gist: Derive reverberation time, clarity and energy decay from measured or simulated impulse responses, and design absorption treatments using image-source or statistical acoustic models.

physics.name: Underwater acoustic propagation modelling
physics.gist: Compute transmission loss in ocean waveguides with normal-mode, ray or parabolic-equation methods for given sound-speed profiles and bathymetry, and invert for environmental parameters.

physics.name: Microphone and hydrophone array source localization
physics.gist: Estimate source directions and positions from multichannel recordings with time-difference-of-arrival estimation, beamforming and subspace methods, including array calibration and resolution analysis.

physics.name: Duct, muffler and acoustic filter design
physics.gist: Model plane-wave propagation in ducts, expansion chambers, resonators and perforates with transfer matrices to compute transmission loss and design silencers to specification.

physics.name: Ultrasonic nondestructive testing signal analysis
physics.gist: Process pulse-echo and guided-wave ultrasonic signals to measure sound speed, attenuation and thickness, and to detect and size flaws with time-of-flight and synthetic-aperture imaging.

physics.name: Laminar incompressible flow simulation
physics.gist: Solve the Navier-Stokes equations for channel, cavity, cylinder or obstacle flows with finite-volume, spectral or lattice-Boltzmann codes to compute drag, separation and vortex shedding.

physics.name: Turbulence statistics from velocity measurements
physics.gist: Analyse hot-wire, LDV or DNS velocity records to compute spectra, structure functions, dissipation rates, integral scales and intermittency, and test them against scaling laws.

physics.name: Particle image velocimetry processing
physics.gist: Cross-correlate particle image pairs to obtain velocity fields with sub-pixel peak fitting, outlier validation and interpolation, then derive vorticity, strain and flow statistics.

physics.name: Shallow-water and free-surface wave modelling
physics.gist: Solve shallow-water, Boussinesq or linear wave equations to model tsunamis, dam breaks, seiches and wave transformation over bathymetry, and analyse wave-gauge records.

physics.name: Boundary layers and potential-flow aerodynamics
physics.gist: Use panel methods, vortex-lattice and integral boundary-layer solvers to compute lift, pressure distributions, transition and skin friction for airfoils and bodies.

physics.name: Monte Carlo of lattice models and critical phenomena
physics.gist: Simulate Ising, Potts, XY or lattice-gas models with Metropolis and cluster algorithms, and extract critical temperatures and exponents by finite-size scaling and histogram reweighting.

physics.name: Langevin and stochastic process modelling
physics.gist: Simulate and analyse Brownian motion, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, escape and first-passage processes, and estimate diffusion and drift parameters from trajectories via Fokker-Planck or likelihood methods.

physics.name: Kinetic Monte Carlo of surface growth and diffusion
physics.gist: Model adsorption, surface diffusion, nucleation and island growth with rate-based kinetic Monte Carlo, and compute roughness scaling, island densities and coverage kinetics.

physics.name: Polymer chain statistics and dynamics
physics.gist: Simulate self-avoiding walks, bead-spring chains or Rouse and Zimm dynamics to compute size scaling, form factors, relaxation spectra and force-extension curves.

physics.name: Phase-field modelling of microstructure evolution
physics.gist: Solve Cahn-Hilliard and Allen-Cahn type equations to simulate spinodal decomposition, coarsening, solidification and grain growth, and measure domain-size kinetics.

physics.name: Finite-difference time-domain electromagnetic simulation
physics.gist: Solve Maxwell's equations on Yee grids with absorbing PML boundaries to compute scattering, transmission, cavity resonances and near-to-far-field patterns of dielectric and metallic structures.

physics.name: Electrostatic and magnetostatic field solving
physics.gist: Solve Laplace and Poisson problems with finite-difference, relaxation or boundary-element methods, and use Biot-Savart integration to compute capacitances, field maps, forces, inductances and coil or electrode designs that meet uniformity targets.

physics.name: Light scattering by particles and plasmonics
physics.gist: Compute extinction, scattering and absorption spectra and angular distributions of spheres, spheroids and clusters with Mie theory, T-matrix or discrete-dipole methods, and invert measured spectra for size distributions or optical constants.

physics.name: Photonic crystal band structure calculation
physics.gist: Compute photonic band diagrams, band gaps and defect modes of 1D-3D periodic dielectric structures with plane-wave expansion or transfer-matrix Bloch methods, and optimise lattice parameters for target gaps.

physics.name: Polarization optics and ellipsometry
physics.gist: Model polarization states and optical elements with Jones and Mueller calculus, and fit ellipsometric Psi-Delta or Mueller-matrix polarimetry data to extract birefringence, optical constants and film parameters.

physics.name: Geometric ray tracing and lens aberration design
physics.gist: Trace real rays through multi-element refractive and reflective systems to evaluate Seidel and higher-order aberrations, spot diagrams and MTF, and optimise curvatures, spacings and glass choices to meet imaging specifications.

physics.name: Photon statistics and quantum optics correlations
physics.gist: Analyse photon time-tag or coincidence data to compute g2 correlation functions, Hong-Ou-Mandel visibilities, squeezing and Fano factors, and model them with cavity-QED or beamsplitter theory.

physics.name: Bose-Einstein condensate Gross-Pitaevskii modelling
physics.gist: Find ground states and simulate dynamics of condensates with imaginary- and real-time Gross-Pitaevskii solvers to study trapped density profiles, vortices, solitons, collective modes and time-of-flight expansion.

physics.name: Tensor network and DMRG simulation of quantum chains
physics.gist: Use matrix-product-state methods such as DMRG and TEBD to compute ground states, entanglement entropy, correlation lengths and quench dynamics of one-dimensional quantum lattice models beyond exact-diagonalization sizes.

physics.name: Variational and diffusion quantum Monte Carlo
physics.gist: Estimate ground-state energies and observables of few-body quantum systems, such as atoms, quantum dots and trapped bosons, with variational and diffusion Monte Carlo using optimised trial wavefunctions and error analysis.

physics.name: Self-consistent mean-field and superconducting gap theory
physics.gist: Solve self-consistent Hartree-Fock, BCS or Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations for lattice and continuum models to obtain order parameters, gap temperature dependence and mean-field phase diagrams, and compare them with tunnelling or thermodynamic data.

physics.name: Quantum well and heterostructure subband modelling
physics.gist: Solve Schrödinger-Poisson and k·p envelope-function equations for semiconductor quantum wells, superlattices and 2D electron gases to obtain subband energies, wavefunctions, charge distributions and intersubband absorption.

physics.name: Mesoscopic quantum transport and Landauer conductance
physics.gist: Compute transmission, conductance quantization, Fabry-Pérot and Aharonov-Bohm interference and shot noise of nanostructures with Landauer-Büttiker and recursive Green's function methods on discretised Hamiltonians.

physics.name: Josephson junction and superconducting circuit dynamics
physics.gist: Simulate RCSJ and SQUID models to obtain I-V characteristics, Shapiro steps, switching distributions and flux modulation, and fit measured junction and SQUID data for critical currents, capacitance and noise.

physics.name: Dielectric and impedance spectroscopy analysis
physics.gist: Fit broadband dielectric and impedance spectra with Debye, Cole-Cole, Havriliak-Negami and equivalent-circuit models, using Kramers-Kronig checks, to extract relaxation times, conductivities and activation energies.

physics.name: Small-angle X-ray and neutron scattering analysis
physics.gist: Reduce and fit SAXS and SANS intensity curves with form-factor and structure-factor models, Guinier and Porod analyses and indirect Fourier transforms to determine particle size, shape, polydispersity and interactions.

physics.name: X-ray absorption and Mössbauer spectroscopy fitting
physics.gist: Extract EXAFS oscillations and fit shell models for coordination numbers and bond lengths, or fit Mössbauer spectra for isomer shifts, quadrupole splittings and hyperfine fields of local environments.

physics.name: Magnetic resonance spin Hamiltonian and relaxation analysis
physics.gist: Simulate and fit EPR and NMR spectra with spin Hamiltonians containing g-tensors, hyperfine and zero-field terms, and analyse relaxation, echo-decay and Bloch-equation data for relaxation times and couplings.

physics.name: Equation-of-state and thermophysical property fitting
physics.gist: Fit Birch-Murnaghan, Vinet, virial or cubic equations of state and Debye-Einstein heat-capacity models to pressure-volume, calorimetric and thermal-expansion data, and derive bulk moduli, phase boundaries and thermodynamic functions.

physics.name: Nuclear structure and mass models
physics.gist: Fit semi-empirical and liquid-drop mass formulas to measured binding energies, and compute single-particle levels in Woods-Saxon or harmonic potentials with spin-orbit coupling to predict shell gaps, separation energies and deformation trends.

physics.name: Charged-particle stopping power and range in matter
physics.gist: Compute energy loss, range, straggling and Bragg curves of ions and electrons with Bethe-Bloch and empirical stopping models, and fit depth-dose or energy-loss measurements for beam and material parameters.

physics.name: Monte Carlo event generation and phase-space integration
physics.gist: Generate weighted and unweighted particle-physics events by sampling multi-body phase space with matrix-element weighting, adaptive (VEGAS-style) integration and detector smearing to compute cross sections and differential distributions.

physics.name: Jet substructure and particle identification
physics.gist: Cluster particles into jets with sequential-recombination algorithms, compute substructure observables, and build cut-based or machine-learning classifiers for flavour and particle identification with efficiency and fake-rate calibration.

physics.name: Lattice field theory Monte Carlo
physics.gist: Simulate scalar phi^4, compact U(1) or SU(2) lattice gauge theories with Metropolis, heat-bath or hybrid Monte Carlo, and measure Wilson loops, string tensions, correlators and masses with autocorrelation-aware errors.

physics.name: Accelerator beam optics and emittance analysis
physics.gist: Compute linear lattice optics with transfer matrices, Twiss parameters, tunes, chromaticity and dispersion for beamlines and rings, and estimate emittance from quadrupole scans or beam-profile measurements.

physics.name: Quantum error correction and circuit simulation
physics.gist: Simulate stabilizer codes and noisy quantum circuits with state-vector or Clifford simulators, decode syndromes, and estimate logical error rates and thresholds under depolarizing, erasure or biased noise models.

physics.name: Compressible gas dynamics and shock waves
physics.gist: Solve the Euler equations with Godunov-type Riemann solvers to simulate shock tubes, nozzle flows, blast waves and shock reflections, and verify results against Rankine-Hugoniot and isentropic relations.

physics.name: Heat conduction, convection and inverse thermal problems
physics.gist: Solve transient conduction and Rayleigh-Bénard or natural-convection problems, compute Nusselt scaling, and infer conductivities, diffusivities or boundary heat fluxes from temperature sensor histories.

physics.name: Stokes flow and microhydrodynamics
physics.gist: Compute low-Reynolds-number flows, drag, mobilities and hydrodynamic interactions of particles, swimmers and microchannels with Stokeslet, boundary-integral and lubrication methods, and compare them with sedimentation or tracking data.

physics.name: Rheology and viscoelastic material characterization
physics.gist: Fit oscillatory-shear, creep, stress-relaxation and flow-curve data with Maxwell, generalized Maxwell, Carreau or Herschel-Bulkley models, building time-temperature superposition master curves and relaxation spectra.

physics.name: Musical and vibrating-system acoustics
physics.gist: Model strings, membranes, bars and air columns, including inharmonicity, bore impedance and radiation, and analyse instrument recordings to extract partials, decay rates and tuning or input-impedance characteristics.

physics.name: Loudspeaker and electroacoustic transducer modelling
physics.gist: Identify Thiele-Small and lumped electro-mechano-acoustic parameters from impedance and response measurements, and design enclosures or transducer networks to target frequency responses.

physics.name: Environmental noise and sound level analysis
physics.gist: Process calibrated sound recordings into frequency-weighted levels, fractional-octave spectra, Leq and percentile statistics, and model outdoor propagation with spreading, ground and barrier attenuation.

physics.name: Precision measurement noise and lock-in analysis
physics.gist: Characterise measurement chains with power spectral densities, Allan variance, digital lock-in demodulation and noise-budget models to separate white, flicker and drift noise and extract weak periodic signals.

physics.name: Active matter and self-propelled particle models
physics.gist: Simulate Vicsek, active Brownian and run-and-tumble particle models to study flocking transitions, motility-induced phase separation and anomalous diffusion, and extract order parameters and phase diagrams.

physics.name: Liquid-state theory and pair correlation analysis
physics.gist: Compute radial distribution functions and structure factors from simulated or measured configurations, and solve Ornstein-Zernike integral equations with closures to predict thermodynamics and compare them with scattering data.

physics.name: Pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems
physics.gist: Simulate Turing, Gray-Scott, Swift-Hohenberg and complex Ginzburg-Landau equations, perform linear stability analysis of homogeneous states, and quantify pattern wavelengths, defects and front speeds.

physics.name: Fusion plasma transport and power balance
physics.gist: Solve 0D and 1D radial transport equations for temperature and density profiles with heating, radiation and confinement scaling laws to assess Lawson criteria, energy confinement times and burn conditions.

physics.name: Bound-state eigenvalue solvers and WKB quantization
physics.gist: Find bound-state energies and eigenfunctions of 1D, radial or coupled-channel potentials with Numerov shooting, finite-difference, DVR or spectral methods, and compare them with WKB and Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization, perturbation theory or measured vibrational levels.

physics.name: Random matrix theory and quantum chaos spectral statistics
physics.gist: Compute level-spacing distributions, spectral rigidity, form factors and eigenvector statistics of quantum billiards, kicked tops or measured resonance spectra after unfolding, and classify them against Poisson, GOE, GUE and GSE ensembles.

physics.name: Anderson localization and disordered electronic systems
physics.gist: Study wave localization in disordered lattices and random media with transfer-matrix, Green's-function and exact-diagonalization methods, extracting localization lengths, inverse participation ratios, mobility edges and critical exponents by finite-size scaling.

physics.name: Percolation theory and cluster statistics
physics.gist: Simulate site, bond and continuum percolation with union-find and Newman-Ziff algorithms, and determine thresholds, cluster-size distributions, fractal dimensions, conductivity exponents and spanning probabilities by finite-size scaling.

physics.name: Driven lattice gases and nonequilibrium steady states
physics.gist: Simulate exclusion processes, zero-range and driven diffusive models with open or periodic boundaries, and compute current-density relations, boundary-induced phase diagrams, density profiles and fluctuation scaling against exact or mean-field results.

physics.name: Rarefied gas dynamics and direct simulation Monte Carlo
physics.gist: Simulate dilute gas flows at finite Knudsen number with DSMC or discrete-velocity Boltzmann solvers to compute Couette and Poiseuille profiles, shock structure, slip, transport coefficients and relaxation to equilibrium.

physics.name: Analytical mechanics and symbolic equations of motion
physics.gist: Derive Lagrangian and Hamiltonian equations of motion, conserved quantities, normal modes, small-oscillation spectra and canonical transformations for constrained mechanical systems symbolically, and verify them numerically.

physics.name: Radiation from accelerated charges and synchrotron emission
physics.gist: Compute Liénard-Wiechert fields, angular power distributions and spectra of radiation from relativistic charges in bending magnets, undulators, Compton and bremsstrahlung geometries, and fit measured emission spectra for beam parameters.

physics.name: Aeroacoustic noise prediction
physics.gist: Predict sound from jets, rotors, fans and flow over edges with Lighthill, Curle and Ffowcs Williams-Hawkings acoustic analogies applied to analytic or simulated source fields, and analyse directivity and tonal versus broadband spectra.

physics.name: Nonlinear acoustics and finite-amplitude waves
physics.gist: Model finite-amplitude sound with Burgers, Westervelt or KZK equations to compute waveform steepening, shock formation, harmonic generation and parametric arrays, and fit nonlinearity and absorption parameters to measured waveforms.

physics.name: Phononic crystals and acoustic metamaterials
physics.gist: Compute band structures, band gaps and effective parameters of periodic elastic and acoustic structures, including locally resonant and negative-index designs, with plane-wave, transfer-matrix or finite-element Bloch methods, and optimise unit cells.

physics.name: Acoustic radiation and scattering by bodies
physics.gist: Solve exterior Helmholtz problems with boundary-element, multipole or modal expansions to compute radiated power, directivity, radiation impedance and scattering cross sections of vibrating pistons, shells and rigid or elastic scatterers.

physics.name: Bubble dynamics and cavitation
physics.gist: Integrate Rayleigh-Plesset, Keller-Miksis and related bubble models to study collapse, acoustic cavitation thresholds, sonoluminescence conditions and bubbly-liquid sound speed, and fit radius-time curves from high-speed imaging.

physics.name: Hydrodynamic linear stability analysis
physics.gist: Solve Orr-Sommerfeld, Rayleigh and related eigenvalue problems with Chebyshev spectral methods for shear flows, jets, wakes and stratified or rotating layers, and obtain neutral curves, critical Reynolds numbers, transient growth and absolute or convective instability.

physics.name: Vortex dynamics and vortex methods
physics.gist: Simulate point-vortex systems, vortex sheets, rings and filaments with Biot-Savart vortex-particle and contour-dynamics methods to study merger, leapfrogging, Kelvin-Helmholtz roll-up and vortex stability.

physics.name: Low-temperature gas discharge modelling
physics.gist: Model glow, RF and DC discharges with global plasma-chemistry models, two-term Boltzmann solvers for electron energy distributions and fluid sheath models to predict Paschen curves, species densities, rate coefficients and power balance.

physics.name: Line-integrated plasma diagnostics and tomographic inversion
physics.gist: Invert chord-integrated interferometry, bolometry, soft-X-ray and emission data with Abel inversion and regularised tomography, and analyse Thomson and collective scattering spectra to obtain local density and temperature profiles.

physics.name: Nuclear reaction cross sections and R-matrix analysis
physics.gist: Compute and fit nuclear reaction cross sections, astrophysical S-factors and resonance parameters with optical-model, Breit-Wigner, R-matrix and Hauser-Feshbach statistical models, and derive thermonuclear reaction rates.

physics.name: Radiation spectrum unfolding and response-matrix inversion
physics.gist: Recover neutron, gamma or charged-particle energy spectra from Bonner-sphere, threshold-foil, scintillator or detector-response measurements with regularised least squares, maximum-entropy, iterative Bayesian and MLEM unfolding with uncertainty propagation.

physics.name: Detector pulse processing and pulse-shape discrimination
physics.gist: Process digitised detector waveforms with trapezoidal and optimal filtering, pile-up rejection, timing pick-off and charge-comparison or machine-learning pulse-shape discrimination to obtain energy, timing resolution and particle-type separation.

physics.name: Perturbative QCD and renormalization-group evolution
physics.gist: Solve renormalization-group equations for running couplings and masses, evolve parton distributions with DGLAP equations, and fit structure-function, event-shape or cross-section data for alpha_s and PDF parameters.

physics.name: Boltzmann transport theory for electrons and phonons
physics.gist: Solve the linearised Boltzmann transport equation in relaxation-time or iterative form for model band structures and phonon dispersions to compute conductivities, Seebeck coefficients, thermoelectric figures of merit and lattice thermal conductivity, and fit them to measurements.

physics.name: Optical response and reflectivity of solids
physics.gist: Fit reflectance, transmittance and absorption spectra of metals, semiconductors and insulators with Drude-Lorentz, Tauc and critical-point models, perform Kramers-Kronig analysis, and extract optical conductivity, band gaps, plasma frequencies and sum-rule weights.

physics.name: Group theory and crystallographic symmetry analysis
physics.gist: Apply point and space group theory, character tables and representation decomposition to classify vibrational and electronic states, derive selection rules, symmetry-adapted Hamiltonians and allowed tensor forms, and identify symmetries of structures.

physics.name: Photoemission spectroscopy analysis
physics.gist: Analyse ARPES intensity maps and XPS or UPS core-level spectra by Fermi-edge calibration, momentum-distribution and energy-distribution curve fitting, and Shirley or Tougaard background subtraction to extract band dispersions, self-energies, work functions and chemical states.

physics.name: Linear spin-wave theory and magnon spectra
physics.gist: Compute magnon dispersions, spin-wave intensities and thermodynamics of ordered magnets with Holstein-Primakoff linear spin-wave theory, and fit exchange and anisotropy constants to inelastic neutron, Brillouin or FMR data.

physics.name: Liquid crystal ordering and director-field modelling
physics.gist: Model nematic, cholesteric and smectic phases with Maier-Saupe, Landau-de Gennes and Frank elasticity, simulating Fréedericksz transitions, defects and switching, and fitting order-parameter, birefringence and electro-optic data.

physics.name: Floquet theory of periodically driven quantum systems
physics.gist: Compute quasienergy spectra, Floquet states, effective Hamiltonians and heating in periodically driven atoms, qubits and lattices, including Landau-Zener-Stückelberg interference, dynamical localization and Floquet topological bands.

physics.name: Laser cooling and atom trapping
physics.gist: Model Doppler, sub-Doppler and sideband cooling, magneto-optical and dipole traps with optical Bloch equations, semiclassical force models and Monte Carlo atom trajectories, and fit time-of-flight, loading and release-recapture data for temperatures and trap parameters.

physics.name: Nonlinear frequency conversion and phase matching
physics.gist: Solve coupled-wave equations for second-harmonic, sum- and difference-frequency generation and optical parametric amplification and oscillation, computing phase-matching angles, quasi-phase-matching periods, acceptance bandwidths and conversion efficiencies from Sellmeier data.

physics.name: Ultrafast pulse characterization
physics.gist: Reconstruct femtosecond pulse amplitude and phase from intensity autocorrelation, FROG, SPIDER or dispersion-scan traces with iterative retrieval algorithms, and design dispersion compensation with prisms, gratings or chirped mirrors.

chemistry.name: Chromatographic peak deconvolution and integration
chemistry.gist: Fit overlapping, tailing GC/HPLC peaks with exponentially modified Gaussian or similar models over drifting baselines to quantify areas, resolution and plate counts.

chemistry.name: Calibration curves and detection limits
chemistry.gist: Build weighted or nonlinear calibration models from standards with heteroscedastic noise, then derive LOD/LOQ, linear range and inverse-predicted concentrations with confidence intervals.

chemistry.name: Mass spectral isotope patterns and formula assignment
chemistry.gist: Compute theoretical isotope distributions and score candidate elemental formulas against high-resolution m/z and intensity data under mass-accuracy constraints.

chemistry.name: LC-MS untargeted feature extraction and alignment
chemistry.gist: Detect chromatographic features in m/z–retention-time data, group adducts and isotopes, correct retention drift across runs and build a feature table.

chemistry.name: Multivariate calibration of NIR spectra
chemistry.gist: Preprocess near-infrared or mid-IR spectra (SNV, derivatives) and build cross-validated PLS or PCR models predicting composition, including outlier and variable selection.

chemistry.name: Multivariate curve resolution of mixture data
chemistry.gist: Decompose spectra-by-time or spectra-by-composition matrices into pure component spectra and concentration profiles using MCR-ALS with nonnegativity and closure constraints.

chemistry.name: Potentiometric titration and pKa determination
chemistry.gist: Model acid-base titration curves of polyprotic species with activity corrections to extract pKa values, endpoints and sample purity.

chemistry.name: Measurement uncertainty budgets for analytical methods
chemistry.gist: Propagate uncertainties from weighing, volumetrics, calibration and recovery through an analytical procedure by GUM linearization and Monte Carlo methods.

chemistry.name: Chromatographic retention modelling and gradient optimization
chemistry.gist: Fit linear-solvent-strength or similar retention models from scouting runs and optimize gradient programs or mobile-phase composition for critical-pair resolution.

chemistry.name: ICP-MS and ICP-OES elemental quantification
chemistry.gist: Process multi-element atomic spectrometry data with internal-standard drift correction, isobaric/spectral interference correction and standard-addition quantification.

chemistry.name: NMR free induction decay processing
chemistry.gist: Convert raw FIDs into quantitative spectra via apodization, zero-filling, Fourier transform, automatic phasing, baseline correction, referencing and peak integration.

chemistry.name: NMR spin system simulation and coupling fitting
chemistry.gist: Simulate strongly coupled multiplets from a spin Hamiltonian and fit chemical shifts and J-couplings to observed 1D spectra.

chemistry.name: NMR relaxation and diffusion inversion
chemistry.gist: Extract T1/T2 relaxation times or diffusion coefficients from multi-exponential decay series (inversion recovery, CPMG, DOSY) with regularized inverse Laplace transforms.

chemistry.name: Vibrational band fitting in IR and Raman spectra
chemistry.gist: Correct fluorescence or scattering baselines and fit Voigt band components to infrared or Raman spectra to quantify species, crystallinity or band shifts.

chemistry.name: Spectrophotometric binding and equilibrium constants
chemistry.gist: Fit UV-Vis titration spectra of host-guest, metal-ligand or acid-base systems to stoichiometric binding models to obtain association constants and species spectra.

chemistry.name: Global analysis of transient absorption data
chemistry.gist: Fit pump-probe time-resolved spectra with kinetic models convolved with an instrument response, including chirp correction, to obtain decay-associated or species-associated spectra.

chemistry.name: Fluorescence lifetimes and quenching analysis
chemistry.gist: Deconvolve time-correlated single-photon counting decays and analyse Stern-Volmer, FRET or anisotropy data to recover lifetimes and quenching constants.

chemistry.name: Rotational spectroscopy line assignment and fitting
chemistry.gist: Assign microwave transitions of asymmetric-top molecules and fit rotational and centrifugal distortion constants of an effective Hamiltonian to measured line frequencies.

chemistry.name: Diatomic rovibrational band analysis
chemistry.gist: Assign P/Q/R branches in rovibrational or electronic band spectra, fit Dunham coefficients and construct potential energy curves by RKR inversion.

chemistry.name: EPR spectrum simulation and hyperfine fitting
chemistry.gist: Simulate continuous-wave EPR spectra of radicals and transition-metal centres from g-tensors and hyperfine couplings and fit them to field-swept derivative data.

chemistry.name: EXAFS and X-ray absorption analysis
chemistry.gist: Normalize X-ray absorption spectra, extract the EXAFS chi(k) signal and fit shell coordination numbers, distances and Debye-Waller factors.

chemistry.name: Powder X-ray diffraction phase analysis
chemistry.gist: Index powder patterns, identify crystalline phases from computed reference patterns and refine lattice parameters, phase fractions and crystallite sizes.

chemistry.name: Kinetic mechanism parameter estimation
chemistry.gist: Fit stiff ODE reaction mechanisms to noisy concentration-time profiles, estimating rate constants with identifiability analysis and discrimination among rival mechanisms.

chemistry.name: Gas-phase combustion mechanism simulation
chemistry.gist: Integrate detailed or reduced combustion mechanisms in constant-volume or flow reactors to compute ignition delays, species profiles and rate sensitivity coefficients.

chemistry.name: Transition state theory and RRKM rate constants
chemistry.gist: Compute thermal and pressure-dependent unimolecular rate constants from molecular parameters using TST, tunnelling corrections and RRKM/master-equation methods.

chemistry.name: Enzyme kinetics and inhibition model fitting
chemistry.gist: Fit Michaelis-Menten, inhibition and multi-substrate rate laws to initial-rate or progress-curve data and discriminate between inhibition mechanisms.

chemistry.name: Stochastic simulation of reaction networks
chemistry.gist: Simulate small-copy-number chemical reaction networks with Gillespie and tau-leaping algorithms and compare fluctuation statistics with chemical master equation solutions.

chemistry.name: Atmospheric photochemical box modelling
chemistry.gist: Integrate tropospheric or chamber chemistry mechanisms with photolysis rates and emissions to simulate ozone, NOx and VOC oxidation and attribute production pathways.

chemistry.name: Thermal analysis kinetics from DSC and TGA
chemistry.gist: Apply isoconversional and model-fitting methods to multi-heating-rate thermogravimetric or calorimetric curves to extract activation energies and reaction models.

chemistry.name: Nonlinear chemical dynamics and oscillating reactions
chemistry.gist: Analyse models of oscillating, bistable or excitable reaction systems through steady-state continuation, bifurcation diagrams and time-series fitting.

chemistry.name: Photochemical kinetics and quantum yields
chemistry.gist: Model photoreaction kinetics under irradiation, including actinometric photon-flux determination, light absorption and inner-filter effects, competing photo- and thermal pathways and photostationary states, to extract quantum yields and rate constants.

chemistry.name: Aqueous speciation and chemical equilibrium computation
chemistry.gist: Solve mass-action and mass-balance systems or minimize Gibbs energy with activity models to compute speciation, solubility and saturation indices of multicomponent solutions.

chemistry.name: Phase equilibria and activity coefficient models
chemistry.gist: Regress NRTL, UNIQUAC or cubic equation-of-state parameters on vapour-liquid or liquid-liquid equilibrium data and compute phase diagrams and azeotropes.

chemistry.name: Statistical thermodynamics from molecular partition functions
chemistry.gist: Compute heat capacities, entropies, equilibrium constants and isotope effects from translational, rotational, vibrational and electronic partition functions.

chemistry.name: Isothermal titration calorimetry analysis
chemistry.gist: Integrate ITC thermograms and fit binding isotherms for single-site, multi-site or competitive models to obtain K, deltaH and stoichiometry with uncertainties.

chemistry.name: Gas adsorption isotherms and porosity
chemistry.gist: Fit Langmuir, BET, Toth or other isotherm models to adsorption data and derive surface areas, pore size distributions and isosteric heats of adsorption.

chemistry.name: Dynamic light scattering size distributions
chemistry.gist: Analyse intensity autocorrelation functions with cumulant and regularized inversion methods to recover hydrodynamic size distributions of colloids and macromolecules.

chemistry.name: Polymerization kinetics and molecular weight distributions
chemistry.gist: Model chain-growth or step-growth polymerization with moment methods or population balances and compare predicted molar mass distributions with GPC data.

chemistry.name: Cyclic voltammetry simulation and mechanism fitting
chemistry.gist: Simulate voltammograms by finite-difference diffusion-reaction models for E, EC or ECE mechanisms and fit rate constants, formal potentials and diffusion coefficients.

chemistry.name: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy fitting
chemistry.gist: Validate impedance spectra with Kramers-Kronig tests, fit equivalent circuits with constant-phase and Warburg elements, or compute distributions of relaxation times.

chemistry.name: Battery cycling and capacity fade analysis
chemistry.gist: Process charge-discharge cycler logs to compute capacity, coulombic efficiency and differential capacity curves, and fit degradation models for state-of-health prediction.

chemistry.name: Tafel and polarization analysis for corrosion and electrocatalysis
chemistry.gist: Fit Butler-Volmer and mass-transport-corrected models to polarization curves to extract exchange currents, Tafel slopes and corrosion rates.

chemistry.name: Pourbaix and predominance diagram construction
chemistry.gist: Compute potential-pH or activity-ratio stability diagrams of elements in aqueous systems from standard thermodynamic data and Nernst equilibria.

chemistry.name: Small-molecule ab initio electronic structure implementation
chemistry.gist: Implement Hartree-Fock, MP2 or configuration interaction on Gaussian basis sets for small molecules and compute energies, dipoles and dissociation curves.

chemistry.name: Hückel and tight-binding models of conjugated systems
chemistry.gist: Build Hückel, PPP or tight-binding Hamiltonians for pi-systems and clusters to predict orbital energies, bond orders, excitation energies and aromaticity indices.

chemistry.name: Potential energy surface fitting and reaction paths
chemistry.gist: Fit analytic or interpolated PESs to ab initio points and locate minima, saddle points and minimum-energy paths by nudged elastic band or string methods.

chemistry.name: Classical molecular dynamics of liquids and solutions
chemistry.gist: Run and analyse force-field MD of molecular liquids and solutions to compute radial distribution functions, diffusion coefficients, viscosities and solvation structure.

chemistry.name: Monte Carlo simulation of molecular fluids and adsorption
chemistry.gist: Perform canonical, grand-canonical or Gibbs-ensemble Monte Carlo of model fluids to compute equations of state, coexistence curves and adsorption uptake.

chemistry.name: Force field parameterization
chemistry.gist: Fit torsional, Lennard-Jones or partial-charge parameters of molecular mechanics force fields to reference energies, forces, electrostatic potentials or liquid properties.

chemistry.name: Harmonic vibrational analysis from Hessians
chemistry.gist: Mass-weight and diagonalize Cartesian Hessians, project out rigid-body motions, and compute normal modes, frequencies, IR intensities and isotope shifts.

chemistry.name: Conformer generation and conformational analysis
chemistry.gist: Enumerate and minimize molecular conformers with RDKit force fields, cluster them, and compute Boltzmann-weighted properties and torsional energy profiles.

chemistry.name: Grid-based quantum dynamics and vibrational eigenstates
chemistry.gist: Solve 1D-2D nuclear Schrödinger equations with DVR or split-operator methods to obtain vibrational levels, tunnelling splittings and wavepacket evolution.

chemistry.name: Quantitative structure-property relationship modelling
chemistry.gist: Compute molecular descriptors or fingerprints and build validated regression or classification models for properties such as solubility, boiling point or toxicity.

chemistry.name: Chemical library filtering and diversity selection
chemistry.gist: Parse, standardize and deduplicate compound collections, apply substructure and property filters, and select diverse or similar subsets by fingerprint similarity.

chemistry.name: Reaction condition optimization and design of experiments
chemistry.gist: Design factorial or response-surface experiments and fit or sequentially optimize yield and selectivity models over temperature, concentration, catalyst and solvent variables.

chemistry.name: NMR-based structure elucidation and candidate ranking
chemistry.gist: Predict chemical shifts for candidate isomers or stereoisomers and rank them against experimental spectra using statistical matching scores.

chemistry.name: Ligand field analysis of transition-metal spectra
chemistry.gist: Assign d-d absorption bands with Tanabe-Sugano or angular overlap models and fit ligand-field splitting and Racah parameters of coordination complexes.

chemistry.name: Magnetic susceptibility and spin Hamiltonian fitting
chemistry.gist: Fit temperature- and field-dependent magnetization data with Curie-Weiss, zero-field-splitting and exchange-coupled spin Hamiltonians for molecular magnets and clusters.

chemistry.name: Molecular point-group symmetry analysis
chemistry.gist: Determine molecular point groups from coordinates and use character tables to classify orbitals and vibrational modes and derive IR/Raman selection rules.

chemistry.name: Coordination geometry and bond valence analysis
chemistry.gist: Analyse crystal structure coordinates to compute coordination numbers, polyhedral distortion indices and bond valence sums for assigning oxidation states.

chemistry.name: Alchemical and umbrella-sampling free energy estimation
chemistry.gist: Estimate solvation, binding or conformational free energies from simulation output using FEP, thermodynamic integration, BAR/MBAR or WHAM, with overlap diagnostics and decorrelation-aware error bars.

chemistry.name: Machine-learned interatomic potentials
chemistry.gist: Train kernel or neural-network potentials on reference energies and forces using atom-centred descriptors. Validate them on held-out configurations and use them in ASE for optimization or dynamics.

chemistry.name: Continuum solvation and Poisson-Boltzmann electrostatics
chemistry.gist: Solve Poisson or Poisson-Boltzmann equations on grids, or apply Born/PCM-type models, to compute solvation energies, electrostatic potentials and pKa shifts of molecules and ions.

chemistry.name: Electron density and population analysis
chemistry.gist: Analyse wavefunctions or cube-file densities to compute Mulliken, Löwdin, Hirshfeld or Bader charges, bond orders, multipole moments and density-difference maps.

chemistry.name: Composite thermochemistry and basis-set extrapolation
chemistry.gist: Combine electronic energies across basis sets and methods with complete-basis-set extrapolation, zero-point and thermal corrections, and isodesmic schemes to predict accurate enthalpies of formation and reaction energies.

chemistry.name: Quasiclassical trajectory reaction dynamics
chemistry.gist: Sample initial conditions and propagate classical trajectories on analytic potential energy surfaces to compute reaction probabilities, cross sections, product state distributions and thermal rate constants.

chemistry.name: Franck-Condon vibronic spectrum simulation
chemistry.gist: Compute Franck-Condon factors in displaced, distorted or Duschinsky-rotated harmonic models to simulate vibronically resolved absorption, emission or photoelectron spectra and fit displacements to measured bands.

chemistry.name: Marcus theory and electron-transfer kinetics
chemistry.gist: Fit driving-force, distance and temperature dependences of electron-transfer rates to Marcus, Marcus-Hush-Chidsey or semiclassical models to extract reorganization energies and electronic couplings.

chemistry.name: Linear free-energy relationships
chemistry.gist: Regress rate and equilibrium data on Hammett, Taft, Brønsted, Swain-Scott or Kamlet-Taft parameters to quantify substituent and solvent effects and diagnose changes in mechanism.

chemistry.name: Group additivity and thermochemical cycles
chemistry.gist: Estimate gas-phase thermochemistry by Benson group additivity and assemble Hess, Born-Haber and bomb-calorimetry cycles with corrections to derive formation enthalpies, bond energies and their uncertainties.

chemistry.name: Single-crystal structure factors and electron density maps
chemistry.gist: Compute structure factors from atomic models and refine positions and displacement parameters against reflection data. Build Patterson, Fourier and difference maps and report R-factors.

chemistry.name: Ionic lattice energies and Ewald summation
chemistry.gist: Compute Madelung constants, lattice energies and defect formation energies of ionic crystals with Ewald or Wolf summation and Born-Mayer repulsion, and compare them with Kapustinskii estimates.

chemistry.name: Solid-state NMR lineshape simulation
chemistry.gist: Simulate static and magic-angle-spinning powder lineshapes with chemical shift anisotropy, dipolar and quadrupolar interactions, and fit tensor parameters to measured spectra.

chemistry.name: Hyperfine-interaction and nuclear probe spectroscopies
chemistry.gist: Analyse, simulate or invert spectra and time signals from local nuclear probes of solids and complexes. Techniques include resonant gamma-ray absorption, nuclear quadrupole resonance, perturbed angular correlation, muon spin rotation/relaxation and nuclear resonant scattering. Results include electric field gradients, hyperfine fields, oxidation and spin states, site populations, magnetic ordering, and temperature or field dependences.

chemistry.name: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy peak fitting
chemistry.gist: Subtract Shirley or Tougaard backgrounds and fit constrained spin-orbit doublets with asymmetric lineshapes to quantify surface chemical states and atomic compositions with sensitivity factors.

chemistry.name: Circular dichroism and chiroptical spectra analysis
chemistry.gist: Deconvolve protein CD spectra into secondary-structure fractions, analyse thermal and chemical denaturation curves, and compare exciton-coupling or computed ECD/VCD spectra to assign absolute configuration.

chemistry.name: Tandem mass spectral matching and fragmentation analysis
chemistry.gist: Preprocess MS/MS spectra, score them against spectral libraries with cosine or entropy similarity, perform in-silico fragmentation and build molecular networks of related compounds.

chemistry.name: Reaction enumeration and template-based retrosynthesis
chemistry.gist: Apply reaction SMARTS templates to enumerate products or virtual libraries, perform atom mapping, and run search-based retrosynthetic expansion with route scoring under building-block constraints.

chemistry.name: Chemical graph enumeration and topological indices
chemistry.gist: Enumerate constitutional isomers and stereoisomers under valence constraints, count them with Pólya methods, and compute Wiener, Randić and other graph invariants for structure-property correlations.

chemistry.name: 3D molecular shape and pharmacophore alignment
chemistry.gist: Generate pharmacophore features and align molecules by shape or feature overlap to compute 3D similarity scores and screen compound sets against query molecules.

chemistry.name: Chemometric classification and sample authentication
chemistry.gist: Build PCA, PLS-DA, SIMCA or one-class models on spectral or compositional fingerprints to classify origin, detect adulteration and estimate class-membership error rates with proper validation.

chemistry.name: Hyperspectral chemical imaging analysis
chemistry.gist: Process Raman, IR or MS imaging cubes by denoising, cosmic-ray and baseline removal, unmixing and clustering to produce component distribution maps and domain statistics.

chemistry.name: Receptor modelling and source apportionment
chemistry.gist: Apply positive matrix factorization, chemical mass balance or other receptor models to multi-species environmental composition data with measurement uncertainties to identify and apportion pollution sources.

chemistry.name: Atomic emission plasma diagnostics
chemistry.gist: Identify lines in LIBS or arc emission spectra, construct Boltzmann and Saha-Boltzmann plots for plasma temperature, use Stark broadening for electron density, and perform calibration-free quantification.

chemistry.name: Electrolyte conductivity and ion transport
chemistry.gist: Fit concentration and temperature dependent conductivity data with Kohlrausch, Debye-Hückel-Onsager or ion-pairing models to obtain limiting molar conductivities, association constants and transference numbers.

chemistry.name: Hydrodynamic voltammetry at rotating electrodes
chemistry.gist: Analyse rotating disk and ring-disk electrode data with Levich and Koutecky-Levich treatments to extract diffusion coefficients, kinetic currents, electron-transfer numbers and intermediate yields.

chemistry.name: Potential-step and current-step transient analysis
chemistry.gist: Fit chronoamperometry, chronocoulometry, chronopotentiometry and GITT transients with Cottrell, Anson, Sand and finite-diffusion models to obtain diffusion coefficients, adsorbed amounts and nucleation parameters.

chemistry.name: Colloidal interactions and electrokinetics
chemistry.gist: Compute DLVO and extended-DLVO interaction potentials, convert electrophoretic mobilities to zeta potentials, and predict aggregation stability ratios as functions of ionic strength and pH.

chemistry.name: Surfactant self-assembly and interfacial tension
chemistry.gist: Determine critical micelle concentrations from tension, conductivity or fluorescence data. Fit Gibbs/Szyszkowski adsorption isotherms and drop-shape profiles to obtain surface excess and interfacial tensions.

chemistry.name: Radiochemical decay chains and nuclear counting statistics
chemistry.gist: Solve Bateman equations for decay and ingrowth chains, deconvolve gamma or alpha spectra with efficiency and dead-time corrections, and compute activities, detection limits and radiometric ages.

chemistry.name: Microkinetic modelling of heterogeneous catalysis
chemistry.gist: Build mean-field surface reaction networks from adsorption and barrier energetics, solve for steady-state coverages and turnover frequencies, and compute degree of rate control, apparent activation energies and scaling-relation volcano plots.

chemistry.name: Lattice kinetic Monte Carlo of surface processes
chemistry.gist: Simulate adsorption, diffusion, reaction and desorption on lattices with rejection-free kinetic Monte Carlo to capture island formation, lateral interactions and deviations from mean-field rates.

chemistry.name: Temperature-programmed desorption and reaction analysis
chemistry.gist: Analyse TPD/TPR spectra with Redhead, leading-edge, heating-rate variation and Polanyi-Wigner fitting to extract desorption orders, activation energies, prefactors and coverage-dependent interactions.

chemistry.name: Kinetic analysis of homogeneous catalytic cycles
chemistry.gist: Convert computed or measured free-energy profiles of homogeneous catalytic cycles into turnover frequencies via energetic span and steady-state microkinetic models, identify TOF-determining states, apply Curtin-Hammett selectivity analysis, and compare competing cycles and ligand variants.

chemistry.name: Graphical kinetic analysis of synthetic reactions
chemistry.gist: Apply reaction progress kinetic analysis, variable time normalization, same-excess experiments and Eyring analysis to in-situ monitoring data to determine catalyst and substrate orders, deactivation and activation parameters.

chemistry.name: Diffusion-controlled reactions and Brownian dynamics
chemistry.gist: Compute Smoluchowski and Debye encounter rates, simulate Brownian dynamics of reacting particles with interaction potentials, and analyse geminate recombination and transient diffusion effects.

chemistry.name: Chemical reactor modelling and residence time distributions
chemistry.gist: Model batch, CSTR, PFR and dispersed-flow reactors with heat effects, analyse tracer RTD data with tanks-in-series or axial-dispersion models, and predict conversion and selectivity under non-ideal mixing.

chemistry.name: Reaction calorimetry and thermal runaway assessment
chemistry.gist: Process heat-flow and adiabatic calorimetry data to obtain reaction enthalpies and heat-release kinetics, and compute adiabatic temperature rise, time to maximum rate and Semenov/Frank-Kamenetskii stability criteria.

chemistry.name: Crystallization and nucleation kinetics
chemistry.gist: Fit classical nucleation and growth rates to induction-time, metastable-zone and particle-size data and simulate batch crystallization with population balance equations and supersaturation control.

chemistry.name: Solid-liquid equilibria and solubility modelling
chemistry.gist: Model temperature- and solvent-dependent solubility with van't Hoff, ideal-solubility and activity-coefficient corrections, and construct eutectic, solid-solution and cocrystal phase diagrams from thermal and solubility data.

chemistry.name: Polymer solution thermodynamics and chain statistics
chemistry.gist: Apply Flory-Huggins and related lattice theories to compute binodals, spinodals and interaction parameters from phase or scattering data, and evaluate chain dimensions with freely jointed, worm-like and rotational-isomeric-state models.

chemistry.name: Intermolecular potentials, virial coefficients and gas transport
chemistry.gist: Fit pair potentials to ab initio or experimental data and compute second and third virial coefficients, Joule-Thomson coefficients and Chapman-Enskog viscosities, diffusivities and thermal conductivities.

chemistry.name: Point-defect chemistry and nonstoichiometry
chemistry.gist: Formulate Kröger-Vink defect equilibria with charge and site balances, solve for defect concentrations versus oxygen partial pressure and doping, and fit Brouwer diagrams to conductivity and nonstoichiometry data.

chemistry.name: Linear-response excited states and UV-Vis spectrum prediction
chemistry.gist: Implement CIS, TDHF/RPA or Tamm-Dancoff response on small molecules to compute excitation energies and oscillator strengths, then broaden them into simulated absorption spectra and compare with experiment.

chemistry.name: Molecular exciton models of aggregates
chemistry.gist: Build Frenkel exciton Hamiltonians from transition dipoles or transition charges for dimers, J/H-aggregates and light-harvesting arrays and predict absorption, CD, delocalization lengths and disorder effects.

chemistry.name: Nonlinear optical spectroscopy response-function simulation
chemistry.gist: Simulate pump-probe, photon-echo and two-dimensional IR or electronic spectra from response functions and lineshape functions (Kubo, Brownian oscillator), and extract spectral diffusion and coupling from measured 2D spectra.

chemistry.name: Line-by-line gas-phase absorption spectroscopy
chemistry.gist: Compute temperature- and pressure-dependent absorption spectra from line lists with Voigt and collisional broadening, and retrieve concentrations, temperatures and line parameters from TDLAS, FTIR or cavity ring-down data.

chemistry.name: Excitation-emission matrix fluorescence and PARAFAC
chemistry.gist: Correct EEM fluorescence data for scatter and inner-filter effects and decompose sample stacks with trilinear PARAFAC models, choosing rank by core consistency and split-half validation to quantify fluorophores.

chemistry.name: Ion mobility spectrometry and collision cross sections
chemistry.gist: Calibrate drift-time or traveling-wave ion mobility data, convert arrival times to collision cross sections, and compute theoretical CCS values from 3D structures with projection or trajectory methods for isomer assignment.

chemistry.name: Capillary electrophoresis mobility analysis
chemistry.gist: Convert migration times to effective mobilities with electroosmotic-flow correction, fit mobility-pH curves for pKa and binding constants, and model peak dispersion and stacking in CE separations.

chemistry.name: X-ray fluorescence quantification
chemistry.gist: Fit energy-dispersive XRF spectra with escape, sum and Compton peaks, and quantify elemental compositions with fundamental-parameter or empirical matrix-effect corrections for absorption and secondary fluorescence.

chemistry.name: Small-angle scattering of nanoparticles and macromolecules
chemistry.gist: Reduce SAXS/SANS curves and fit Guinier, Porod and form-factor/structure-factor models or indirect Fourier transforms to determine sizes, shapes, polydispersity and pair distance distributions.

chemistry.name: Stable isotope ratio analysis and fractionation
chemistry.gist: Convert raw isotope-ratio measurements to delta values with reference-material normalization, and apply Rayleigh fractionation, isotope mixing models and equilibrium fractionation factors to trace sources and processes.

chemistry.name: Gas-particle partitioning and aerosol thermodynamics
chemistry.gist: Model secondary organic aerosol formation with volatility basis sets and absorptive partitioning, fit thermodenuder or chamber yield data, and compute inorganic aerosol equilibria and hygroscopic growth.

chemistry.name: Multimedia environmental fate modelling
chemistry.gist: Build Mackay-type fugacity models across air, water, soil and sediment compartments from partition coefficients and degradation rates to predict steady-state and dynamic distributions, persistence and transport potential.

chemistry.name: Continuum modelling of electrochemical devices
chemistry.gist: Transport-reaction models of working electrochemical cells such as batteries, fuel cells, water electrolysers, supercapacitors, redox-flow cells and electrodialysis stacks. Tasks couple species and charge transport, interfacial kinetics, heat generation and current distribution to simulate polarization, discharge or thermal behaviour. They also estimate transport, kinetic and ohmic parameters from cell data, or optimize electrode geometry and operating conditions against performance targets.

chemistry.name: Semiconductor electrochemistry and Mott-Schottky analysis
chemistry.gist: Analyse capacitance-potential and photocurrent data of semiconductor electrodes to obtain flat-band potentials, dopant densities, band-edge positions and charge-transfer versus recombination efficiencies.

chemistry.name: Pulse and stripping voltammetry
chemistry.gist: Simulate and analyse differential-pulse, square-wave and anodic or adsorptive stripping voltammograms to resolve overlapping peaks, extract kinetic parameters and quantify trace analytes.

chemistry.name: Molecular docking and scoring
chemistry.gist: Prepare receptor grids and ligand conformers, implement or apply empirical scoring functions with pose search, and evaluate pose reproduction, enrichment and score-affinity correlation on benchmark ligand sets.

chemistry.name: Search-based molecular design and optimization
chemistry.gist: Optimize molecules for property objectives with genetic algorithms, fragment growing or Monte Carlo tree search over SMILES or graphs using RDKit, under synthesizability, similarity and multi-objective constraints.

materials-science.name: Powder X-ray diffraction phase identification
materials-science.gist: Index and match peaks in simulated or measured powder XRD patterns against candidate crystal structures to identify phases and estimate their fractions.

materials-science.name: Rietveld-style whole-pattern refinement
materials-science.gist: Fit lattice parameters, atomic positions, thermal factors and peak-shape parameters to a full diffraction profile by nonlinear least squares.

materials-science.name: Crystallite size and microstrain from line broadening
materials-science.gist: Separate instrumental, size and strain contributions to diffraction peak widths using Scherrer, Williamson-Hall or Warren-Averbach analysis.

materials-science.name: Space group and symmetry analysis
materials-science.gist: Determine point and space groups, Wyckoff positions and symmetry-equivalent sites from atomic coordinates, with tolerance handling for distorted structures.

materials-science.name: Crystal structure generation and supercells
materials-science.gist: Build bulk, supercell, slab, interface and defect structures from CIF-like inputs and compute coordination, bond lengths and densities.

materials-science.name: Texture and orientation distribution analysis
materials-science.gist: Compute pole figures, orientation distribution functions and texture indices from simulated EBSD orientations or diffraction intensities.

materials-science.name: EBSD map processing and grain reconstruction
materials-science.gist: Segment orientation maps into grains by misorientation thresholds, clean bad pixels, and compute grain sizes, boundary character and KAM.

materials-science.name: Grain size and microstructure image quantification
materials-science.gist: Segment micrograph images to measure grain size distributions, phase area fractions and particle morphology following stereological methods.

materials-science.name: Stereology and 3D microstructure statistics
materials-science.gist: Infer 3D particle size distributions and two-point correlation functions from 2D sections or tomographic voxel volumes.

materials-science.name: Phase-field simulation of microstructure evolution
materials-science.gist: Solve Cahn-Hilliard or Allen-Cahn equations for spinodal decomposition, coarsening or grain growth and extract characteristic length-scale kinetics.

materials-science.name: Monte Carlo Potts grain growth
materials-science.gist: Simulate grain growth or recrystallization on lattices with Potts models and compare growth exponents and size distributions with theory.

materials-science.name: CALPHAD thermodynamic modelling and assessment
materials-science.gist: Minimize Gibbs energies of solution and compound phases with Redlich-Kister models to compute binary or ternary phase equilibria and tie lines, and fit excess Gibbs energy parameters to enthalpy of mixing, activity and phase-boundary data with uncertainty estimates.

materials-science.name: Solidification and segregation modelling
materials-science.gist: Model solute redistribution with Scheil, lever-rule or back-diffusion models and predict microsegregation profiles and solidification paths.

materials-science.name: Diffusion in solids and interdiffusion profiles
materials-science.gist: Solve or invert Fickian and concentration-dependent diffusion problems, e.g. Boltzmann-Matano analysis of diffusion-couple profiles.

materials-science.name: Precipitation kinetics and JMAK transformation
materials-science.gist: Fit Avrami/JMAK or Kampmann-Wagner nucleation-growth-coarsening models to transformed-fraction or particle-size data from heat treatments.

materials-science.name: Steel heat treatment and hardenability
materials-science.gist: Predict phase fractions, CCT/TTT behaviour and hardness profiles from composition and cooling history using empirical and kinetic models.

materials-science.name: Alloy composition design and screening
materials-science.gist: Search compositional spaces for alloys meeting targets using empirical rules (VEC, mismatch, mixing entropy) and surrogate models with constraints.

materials-science.name: Tensile test curve analysis
materials-science.gist: Extract modulus, yield strength, UTS, uniform elongation and hardening parameters from noisy stress-strain data with compliance correction.

materials-science.name: Constitutive plasticity model calibration
materials-science.gist: Fit Johnson-Cook, Voce, Chaboche or similar hardening and rate-dependent models to multi-condition mechanical test data.

materials-science.name: Fatigue life and S-N analysis
materials-science.gist: Fit Basquin, Coffin-Manson and mean-stress-corrected models to cyclic test data with run-outs, and estimate life distributions.

materials-science.name: Fracture mechanics and crack growth
materials-science.gist: Compute stress intensity factors, J-integrals and Paris-law crack growth predictions from geometry, loading and test data.

materials-science.name: Creep and stress rupture modelling
materials-science.gist: Fit Norton power-law, Larson-Miller and theta-projection models to creep curves and extrapolate long-term rupture behaviour.

materials-science.name: Nanoindentation data analysis
materials-science.gist: Apply Oliver-Pharr analysis with area-function and drift correction to load-displacement curves to obtain hardness and modulus maps.

materials-science.name: Weibull strength statistics of brittle materials
materials-science.gist: Estimate Weibull parameters from fracture strength data with censoring and size effects and predict component failure probabilities.

materials-science.name: Viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanical analysis
materials-science.gist: Fit Prony series or fractional models to relaxation and DMA data and build master curves via time-temperature superposition.

materials-science.name: Homogenization of composite elastic properties
materials-science.gist: Compute effective stiffness of composites and porous materials using Mori-Tanaka, self-consistent schemes, bounds or FFT-based solvers on voxel microstructures.

materials-science.name: Laminate and fibre composite mechanics
materials-science.gist: Apply classical lamination theory and failure criteria to compute laminate stiffness, ply stresses and optimal stacking sequences.

materials-science.name: Finite element analysis of material specimens
materials-science.gist: Solve 2D elasticity or thermo-mechanical problems for specimens and microstructures with simple FE codes to obtain stress concentrations and fields.

materials-science.name: Residual stress from diffraction strain
