civil-engineering.name: Traffic state estimation from detector data
civil-engineering.gist: Reconstruct space-time speed and density fields and travel times from loop detector, probe vehicle or Bluetooth data using filtering and interpolation methods.

civil-engineering.name: Car-following model calibration
civil-engineering.gist: Calibrate microscopic car-following and lane-changing models such as IDM or Gipps on vehicle trajectory data, and analyse stop-and-go wave propagation and string stability.

civil-engineering.name: Traffic signal timing optimization
civil-engineering.gist: Optimize cycle lengths, splits and offsets for isolated and coordinated intersections using delay models, queue simulation and mathematical programming.

civil-engineering.name: Network traffic assignment and demand modelling
civil-engineering.gist: Estimate origin-destination demand and solve user-equilibrium or stochastic assignment on road networks to evaluate link flows and infrastructure changes.

civil-engineering.name: Road safety and crash data analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Fit count-data safety performance functions, identify crash hotspots with empirical Bayes methods, and estimate crash-modification factors from before-after data.

civil-engineering.name: Public transit scheduling and network design
civil-engineering.gist: Optimize routes, frequencies, timetables and vehicle or crew schedules for bus and rail systems using integer programming and heuristics on synthetic GTFS-like data.

civil-engineering.name: Pavement performance and deterioration modelling
civil-engineering.gist: Model the progression of roughness, rutting and cracking from pavement management data with regression, survival or Markov models, and optimize maintenance timing.

civil-engineering.name: Mechanistic-empirical pavement analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Compute stresses and strains in layered elastic pavement systems under traffic loads, back-calculate layer moduli from deflection tests and predict fatigue and rutting damage.

civil-engineering.name: Concrete mix design and strength prediction
civil-engineering.gist: Proportion concrete mixtures to strength, workability and durability targets, and model the development of compressive strength from mix composition and curing data.

civil-engineering.name: Cement hydration and temperature development
civil-engineering.gist: Model heat of hydration, maturity and early-age temperature fields in mass concrete pours to predict strength gain and thermal cracking risk.

civil-engineering.name: Asphalt viscoelastic characterization
civil-engineering.gist: Construct dynamic modulus and phase-angle master curves for asphalt binders and mixtures using time-temperature superposition, sigmoidal fits and Prony-series conversion.

civil-engineering.name: Chloride ingress and reinforcement corrosion
civil-engineering.gist: Fit diffusion models to chloride profiles, predict corrosion initiation and propagation under uncertainty, and estimate the service life of reinforced concrete structures.

civil-engineering.name: Creep and shrinkage of concrete
civil-engineering.gist: Calibrate creep and shrinkage prediction models such as B4 or Model Code formulations on test data, and compute long-term deflections and prestress losses in structures.

civil-engineering.name: Nondestructive testing signal analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Process ultrasonic, impact-echo, acoustic-emission or ground-penetrating radar signals to locate defects, estimate thickness and map material condition in concrete and steel elements.

civil-engineering.name: Construction scheduling and resource optimization
civil-engineering.gist: Build critical-path schedules, perform resource leveling and time-cost trade-off optimization, and run Monte Carlo risk analysis on project durations and costs.

civil-engineering.name: Hydraulic transients and water hammer
civil-engineering.gist: Simulate pressure surges in pipelines and pumping mains with the method of characteristics for valve closures, pump trips and column separation, and size surge protection such as air vessels and surge tanks.

civil-engineering.name: Regional groundwater flow modelling and calibration
civil-engineering.gist: Build finite-difference or finite-element steady and transient groundwater flow models with recharge, rivers and wells, calibrate conductivity zones or pilot points to head and baseflow observations, and quantify predictive uncertainty.

civil-engineering.name: Snow accumulation and melt modelling
civil-engineering.gist: Estimate snow water equivalent and meltwater runoff from station or gridded meteorology with degree-day and energy-balance snowpack models, calibrated against snow-pillow, snow-course or snow-cover data.

civil-engineering.name: Drought indices and low-flow frequency analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Compute meteorological and hydrological drought indices such as SPI, SPEI and streamflow deficits, characterize drought duration and severity, and estimate low-flow statistics like 7Q10 for water-supply and permitting design.

civil-engineering.name: Two-dimensional flood inundation modelling
civil-engineering.gist: Solve depth-averaged shallow-water or diffusive-wave equations on DEM grids to map floodplain inundation depth, velocity and arrival time, and compare simulated extents with observed flood maps.

civil-engineering.name: Drinking water treatment and disinfection modelling
civil-engineering.gist: Model coagulation, sedimentation, filtration, adsorption and disinfection processes, including CT compliance, chlorine and chloramine decay kinetics and disinfection by-product formation, fitted to jar-test and plant data.

civil-engineering.name: Contaminated site human-health risk assessment
civil-engineering.gist: Quantify exposure through soil, groundwater, vapour-intrusion and food pathways, compute hazard quotients and cancer risks with probabilistic Monte Carlo methods, and back-calculate risk-based cleanup targets.

civil-engineering.name: Solid waste collection and facility planning
civil-engineering.gist: Optimize waste collection routes, transfer-station and treatment-facility siting, and material-recovery flows using vehicle-routing, location-allocation and mixed-integer programming on generation and composition data.

civil-engineering.name: Rock mass characterization and rock slope stability
civil-engineering.gist: Analyse discontinuity orientations with stereographic and kinematic methods, compute rock mass ratings and Hoek-Brown parameters, and evaluate planar, wedge and toppling failures deterministically and probabilistically.

civil-engineering.name: Surface-wave and ambient-noise site characterization
civil-engineering.gist: Extract dispersion curves from MASW or array microtremor records and horizontal-to-vertical spectral ratios, then invert them for layered shear-wave velocity profiles and site parameters such as Vs30 and fundamental frequency.

civil-engineering.name: Ground improvement design and verification
civil-engineering.gist: Design stone columns, deep soil mixing, dynamic compaction, grouting and wick-drain preloading schemes, and verify their effectiveness from pre- and post-improvement in situ tests and settlement records.

civil-engineering.name: Rainfall-induced landslides and debris-flow runout
civil-engineering.gist: Derive rainfall intensity-duration thresholds from landslide inventories, compute physically based infinite-slope susceptibility maps, and simulate debris-flow and rock-avalanche runout distance and velocity with depth-averaged or energy-line models.

civil-engineering.name: Dynamic soil-structure interaction and machine foundations
civil-engineering.gist: Compute frequency-dependent foundation impedance functions, kinematic and inertial interaction effects, and the vibration response of machine foundations and embedded structures on layered soil.

civil-engineering.name: Buckling and stability of steel members
civil-engineering.gist: Determine elastic and inelastic buckling loads, lateral-torsional and local or distortional buckling of columns, beams and thin-walled sections using eigenvalue analysis, finite-strip methods and imperfection-sensitive nonlinear analysis.

civil-engineering.name: Structural fire engineering
civil-engineering.gist: Model fire exposure with standard and parametric time-temperature curves, solve transient heat transfer into steel, concrete and timber sections, and evaluate degraded member capacity and fire-resistance time.

civil-engineering.name: Cable and tensile structure form finding
civil-engineering.gist: Find equilibrium shapes and prestress states of cable nets, membranes and cable-stayed or suspension bridges with force-density and dynamic-relaxation methods, then analyse their geometrically nonlinear response to load.

civil-engineering.name: Masonry and arch structure analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Assess masonry arches, vaults and walls with thrust-line and limit analysis, rigid-block mechanisms and no-tension material models to obtain collapse loads and safety factors for historic structures.

civil-engineering.name: Vehicle-bridge interaction dynamics
civil-engineering.gist: Simulate coupled dynamics of moving vehicles or trains and bridge decks with road-roughness excitation to compute dynamic amplification factors, resonance speeds and deck accelerations, and to identify bridge properties from vehicle response.

civil-engineering.name: Blast and impact loading of structures
civil-engineering.gist: Derive blast pressure-impulse histories from scaled-distance relations and analyse structural members with equivalent SDOF and multi-degree models to build pressure-impulse diagrams and damage assessments.

civil-engineering.name: Geodetic survey network adjustment and deformation analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Perform least-squares adjustment of levelling, total-station and GNSS networks, detect blunders with statistical testing, and identify significant displacements of dams, bridges and slopes between monitoring epochs.

civil-engineering.name: Point-cloud processing for infrastructure inspection
civil-engineering.gist: Register, segment and fit geometric primitives to terrestrial or airborne laser-scanning point clouds to extract as-built geometry, tunnel ovalization, bridge clearances, surface defects and deformations relative to design models.

civil-engineering.name: Travel mode and destination choice modelling
civil-engineering.gist: Estimate multinomial, nested and mixed logit models on revealed or stated-preference survey data to derive values of travel time and elasticities, and forecast responses to pricing and service changes.

civil-engineering.name: Highway geometric design and alignment optimization
civil-engineering.gist: Design and check horizontal and vertical alignments, superelevation, sight distances and cross-sections against design standards, and optimize alignments over terrain for cost and earthwork balance.

civil-engineering.name: Pedestrian and crowd dynamics
civil-engineering.gist: Simulate pedestrian movement and building or station evacuation with social-force, cellular-automaton or macroscopic models, and calibrate speed-density relations and bottleneck flows from trajectory data.

civil-engineering.name: Railway track geometry and degradation analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Process track recording-car geometry signals to compute standard deviations and defect indicators, model track settlement and degradation over tonnage, and plan tamping and renewal interventions.

civil-engineering.name: Infrastructure network resilience and interdependency
civil-engineering.gist: Model transport, water and power networks as graphs, simulate cascading failures under hazard scenarios, compute resilience and functionality-recovery metrics, and optimize restoration sequencing.

civil-engineering.name: Construction material microstructure image analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Segment X-ray CT, SEM and optical images of concrete, asphalt and soils to quantify air voids, aggregate gradation and orientation, cracks and pore connectivity, and relate them to measured properties.

civil-engineering.name: Precipitation field estimation and radar-gauge merging
civil-engineering.gist: Combine rain-gauge records with weather-radar or satellite estimates through bias correction, kriging with external drift and conditional merging, and derive areal reduction factors and catchment rainfall.

civil-engineering.name: Tidal analysis and estuarine salinity intrusion
civil-engineering.gist: Perform harmonic tidal analysis of water-level records, predict storm surge residuals, and model tidal propagation and salt-wedge intrusion in estuaries with one-dimensional hydrodynamic and advection-dispersion models.

civil-engineering.name: Air quality data analysis and source apportionment
civil-engineering.gist: Analyse monitored particulate and gaseous pollutant concentrations with receptor models such as positive matrix factorization and chemical mass balance, together with trend and meteorological-normalization analysis.

civil-engineering.name: Probabilistic seismic hazard analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Compute site hazard curves and uniform-hazard spectra by integrating earthquake source models, magnitude-recurrence relations and ground-motion models, then perform deaggregation and logic-tree treatment of epistemic uncertainty.

civil-engineering.name: Plate, shell and slab structural analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Analyse bending and membrane action of plates, slabs and thin shells with Kirchhoff/Mindlin finite elements, finite differences or yield-line theory to obtain deflections, moment fields and collapse loads.

civil-engineering.name: Timber and engineered wood structures
civil-engineering.gist: Model moisture-dependent stiffness, mechano-sorptive creep, connection slip and duration-of-load effects in solid timber, glulam and CLT members, and check them against serviceability and strength criteria.

civil-engineering.name: FRP strengthening and retrofit of structures
civil-engineering.gist: Design and evaluate externally bonded or near-surface-mounted fibre-reinforced polymer strengthening of beams, slabs and columns, including bond-slip and debonding models fitted to test data and confinement models.

civil-engineering.name: Fracture mechanics of concrete and quasi-brittle materials
civil-engineering.gist: Fit cohesive-crack softening laws and size-effect models to notched-beam and splitting tests, and simulate crack propagation and fracture energy dissipation in concrete and rock-like materials.

civil-engineering.name: Asphalt mixture volumetric design and aggregate blending
civil-engineering.gist: Blend aggregate stockpiles to target gradations, compute air voids, VMA and VFA from specific-gravity data, and select optimum binder content under Superpave or Marshall design criteria.

civil-engineering.name: Construction materials acceptance and quality control
civil-engineering.gist: Apply statistical acceptance plans, percent-within-limits pay factors, control charts and compaction data analysis to field and laboratory test results for concrete, asphalt and earthworks.

civil-engineering.name: Geosynthetics and reinforced soil structures
civil-engineering.gist: Design mechanically stabilized earth walls, reinforced slopes and geosynthetic-reinforced embankments by checking internal and external stability, reinforcement strains and long-term creep reduction.

civil-engineering.name: Frozen ground and permafrost geotechnics
civil-engineering.gist: Solve heat conduction with phase change in soils to predict frost penetration, thaw settlement and frost heave beneath roads, pipelines and foundations, and design insulation or thermosyphon mitigation.

civil-engineering.name: Energy geostructures and ground heat exchangers
civil-engineering.gist: Simulate heat transfer around energy piles and borehole heat exchangers with line-source and g-function models, interpret thermal response tests and assess thermally induced pile stresses.

civil-engineering.name: Dam safety monitoring and stability analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Model dam displacements, piezometric levels and seepage from monitoring records with hydrostatic-season-time regression, and evaluate sliding, overturning and uplift stability of gravity and embankment dams.

civil-engineering.name: Stage-discharge rating curves and streamflow measurement
civil-engineering.gist: Process current-meter and ADCP gauging data, fit segmented power-law rating curves with hysteresis and shifts, and quantify streamflow uncertainty with Bayesian rating-curve methods.

civil-engineering.name: DEM-based terrain and watershed analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Delineate catchments and stream networks from digital elevation models through pit filling, flow-direction and flow-accumulation algorithms, and derive geomorphometric indices such as topographic wetness and hypsometry.

civil-engineering.name: Event-based runoff and unit hydrograph methods
civil-engineering.gist: Derive unit and synthetic hydrographs, apply SCS curve-number, rational and Green-Ampt loss methods, and compute design-storm flood hydrographs and their routing through reservoirs and channels.

civil-engineering.name: Hydrologic forecasting and data assimilation
civil-engineering.gist: Produce deterministic and ensemble streamflow forecasts by updating hydrological model states with Kalman or particle filters, and verify forecast skill with probabilistic scores.

civil-engineering.name: Hydraulic structure design
civil-engineering.gist: Size culverts, weirs, spillways, stilling basins and energy dissipators from discharge and tailwater conditions, computing head-discharge relations, hydraulic jumps and cavitation and scour risk.

civil-engineering.name: Statistical downscaling and bias correction of climate projections
civil-engineering.gist: Downscale and bias-correct climate-model temperature and precipitation with quantile mapping, delta change and regression methods, and propagate the corrected scenarios into hydrological impact assessments.

civil-engineering.name: Trend and change-point detection in hydroclimatic records
civil-engineering.gist: Detect monotonic trends, abrupt shifts and homogeneity breaks in streamflow, rainfall and temperature series with Mann-Kendall, Pettitt and related tests that account for serial correlation and field significance.

civil-engineering.name: Multivariate and compound hydrologic hazard analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Fit copula models to jointly distributed flood peaks, volumes, durations, storm surge and rainfall to estimate joint and conditional return periods and compound-flood design events.

civil-engineering.name: Stochastic weather and streamflow generation
civil-engineering.gist: Build Markov-chain, autoregressive and resampling generators of daily rainfall, temperature and multisite streamflow that reproduce observed statistics, for use in long-term risk and design studies.

civil-engineering.name: Environmental flows and ecohydraulics
civil-engineering.gist: Combine hydraulic simulations with habitat suitability curves to compute weighted usable area, apply hydrologic-alteration indicators and design environmental flow regimes below dams and diversions.

civil-engineering.name: Soil erosion and catchment sediment yield
civil-engineering.gist: Estimate hillslope soil loss and sediment delivery with USLE/RUSLE-type and process-based erosion models using rainfall erosivity, soil, slope and land-cover data, and calibrate them to sediment-yield records.

civil-engineering.name: Soil and groundwater remediation design
civil-engineering.gist: Design and optimize pump-and-treat capture zones, permeable reactive barriers, soil vapour extraction and in situ bioremediation systems using flow, mass-transfer and degradation-kinetics models.

civil-engineering.name: Quantitative microbial risk assessment
civil-engineering.gist: Estimate pathogen exposure and infection risk from drinking water, recreational water and wastewater reuse with dose-response models, log-removal credits and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis.

civil-engineering.name: Environmental noise prediction and mapping
civil-engineering.gist: Predict road, rail and construction noise levels with standard propagation models, compute Leq and Lden indicators at receivers and design noise barriers to meet exposure limits.

civil-engineering.name: Traffic emissions and vehicle energy estimation
civil-engineering.gist: Estimate fuel use, CO2 and pollutant emissions from speed and acceleration trajectories or link flows with vehicle-specific-power and modal emission models, and compare traffic management scenarios.

civil-engineering.name: Airport airside capacity and operations
civil-engineering.gist: Compute runway capacity from separation rules and fleet mix, simulate arrival and departure queues and delays, and analyse gate assignment and apron operations.

civil-engineering.name: Construction operations discrete-event simulation
civil-engineering.gist: Simulate earthmoving, concrete placement and other cyclic construction operations as queueing networks to estimate productivity, optimize equipment fleet sizes and balance haul cycles.

civil-engineering.name: Construction cost estimation and earned value analysis
civil-engineering.gist: Develop parametric cost estimates from historical project data and track cost and schedule performance with earned value indices, forecasting completion cost and detecting overruns.

civil-engineering.name: Buried pipe failure prediction and renewal planning
civil-engineering.gist: Model water main and sewer pipe break rates and condition deterioration with survival, Poisson and Markov models fitted to asset records, and optimize rehabilitation and replacement timing under budget constraints.

statistics.name: Generalized linear models for counts
statistics.gist: Fit Poisson, negative binomial and zero-inflated regressions to overdispersed count data with exposure offsets, compare them by deviance and AIC, and report rate ratios with confidence intervals.

statistics.name: Logistic regression and calibration
statistics.gist: Fit binary-outcome models with interactions or splines, assess discrimination (AUC) and calibration (reliability curves, Hosmer-Lemeshow), and recalibrate predicted risks.

statistics.name: Linear mixed-effects models
statistics.gist: Fit random-intercept and random-slope models to nested or crossed grouped data by REML, estimate variance components and intraclass correlations, and test fixed effects.

statistics.name: Generalized additive models and splines
statistics.gist: Model smooth nonlinear covariate effects with penalized regression splines, choose smoothing by GCV or REML, and report effective degrees of freedom and fitted curves.

statistics.name: Robust and quantile regression
statistics.gist: Estimate conditional medians and quantiles or use M-estimators on heavy-tailed, outlier-contaminated data, and compare the results with OLS together with bootstrap uncertainty.

statistics.name: Regression diagnostics and influence analysis
statistics.gist: Detect heteroscedasticity, leverage points, multicollinearity and misspecification using residual tests, Cook's distance and VIF, then apply corrections such as sandwich standard errors or transformations.

statistics.name: High-dimensional penalized regression
statistics.gist: Fit lasso, elastic net and ridge models to p >> n data, tune penalties by cross-validation, and assess variable-selection stability or post-selection inference.

statistics.name: Nonlinear least squares curve fitting
statistics.gist: Fit mechanistic parametric curves (dose-response, growth, decay kinetics) by nonlinear least squares, derive parameter confidence intervals by profiling or the delta method, and check identifiability.

statistics.name: Measurement error and errors-in-variables
statistics.gist: Correct regression estimates for covariate measurement error using Deming regression, regression calibration or SIMEX, with replicate or validation data.

statistics.name: Bootstrap and resampling inference
statistics.gist: Build percentile, BCa and studentized bootstrap or jackknife confidence intervals for complex statistics, including block bootstraps for dependent data.

statistics.name: Permutation and rank-based tests
statistics.gist: Run exact or Monte Carlo permutation tests and nonparametric rank procedures (Wilcoxon, Kruskal-Wallis, Friedman) with ties and stratification, and report p-values and effect sizes.

statistics.name: Multiple testing and false discovery control
statistics.gist: Apply Bonferroni, Holm, Benjamini-Hochberg, Storey q-values and hierarchical FDR procedures to large families of tests, and estimate the proportion of true nulls.

statistics.name: Likelihood inference and profile likelihood
statistics.gist: Derive and maximize custom likelihoods, compute Wald, score and likelihood-ratio tests and profile-likelihood intervals, and handle boundary parameters.

statistics.name: Contingency tables and categorical data
statistics.gist: Analyse multiway tables with log-linear models, Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel tests, exact tests and ordinal association measures, and summarize the dependence structure.

statistics.name: Ordinal and multinomial response models
statistics.gist: Fit proportional-odds, partial proportional-odds and multinomial logit models to ordered or nominal outcomes, test the proportional-odds assumption and report predicted category probabilities.

statistics.name: Bayesian hierarchical modelling with MCMC
statistics.gist: Write and run Gibbs or Metropolis-Hastings samplers (or use available PPL tools) for multilevel models, check convergence with R-hat and ESS, and summarize partial pooling.

statistics.name: Conjugate and empirical Bayes analysis
statistics.gist: Derive closed-form posteriors or estimate prior hyperparameters from many parallel units (beta-binomial, gamma-Poisson shrinkage) to produce shrunken estimates and credible intervals.

statistics.name: Bayesian model comparison and evidence
statistics.gist: Compute marginal likelihoods, Bayes factors, WAIC and PSIS-LOO by bridge sampling, Laplace approximation or thermodynamic integration, and rank competing models.

statistics.name: Variational and Laplace approximate inference
statistics.gist: Implement mean-field variational Bayes or Laplace/INLA-style approximations for latent-variable models, and benchmark their accuracy against long MCMC runs.

statistics.name: Posterior predictive model checking
statistics.gist: Simulate replicated data from fitted Bayesian models, compute discrepancy statistics and calibrated posterior predictive p-values, and run simulation-based calibration of inference code.

statistics.name: Bayesian nonparametrics and mixture models
statistics.gist: Fit finite and Dirichlet-process mixtures with EM or collapsed Gibbs sampling, infer the number of clusters, and handle label switching in posterior summaries.

statistics.name: ARIMA and seasonal time series forecasting
statistics.gist: Identify, fit and diagnose SARIMA models on univariate series with trends, seasonality and calendar effects, and produce forecasts with prediction intervals and rolling-origin evaluation.

statistics.name: State space models and Kalman smoothing
statistics.gist: Cast structural time series (local level, trend, seasonal, regression) in state space form, estimate parameters by maximum likelihood with the Kalman filter, and extract smoothed components.

statistics.name: Volatility and GARCH modelling
statistics.gist: Fit GARCH, EGARCH and GJR models with heavy-tailed innovations to return series, forecast conditional variance, and backtest value-at-risk.

statistics.name: Vector autoregression and cointegration
statistics.gist: Fit VAR and VECM models to multivariate series, select lag order, run Granger causality and Johansen tests, and compute impulse responses and variance decompositions.

statistics.name: Change-point and structural break detection
statistics.gist: Locate abrupt shifts in mean, variance or regression structure using PELT, binary segmentation, CUSUM or Bayesian online methods, and quantify uncertainty in break locations.

statistics.name: Spectral analysis of time series
statistics.gist: Estimate power spectra with periodograms, Welch and multitaper methods, handle unevenly sampled series via Lomb-Scargle, and test the significance of periodicities.

statistics.name: Hierarchical and grouped forecast reconciliation
statistics.gist: Produce coherent forecasts across aggregation hierarchies (regions, products, temporal levels) with bottom-up, MinT or OLS reconciliation, and evaluate accuracy at every level.

statistics.name: Intermittent and count time series
statistics.gist: Model sparse demand or event-count series with Croston-type methods, INAR or Poisson autoregressions, and evaluate the forecasts with scale-free error metrics.

statistics.name: Long memory and fractional processes
statistics.gist: Estimate the Hurst exponent and fractional differencing parameter with R/S, DFA, GPH or Whittle estimators, and fit ARFIMA models to persistent series.

statistics.name: Kaplan-Meier and nonparametric survival
statistics.gist: Estimate survival curves under right censoring and left truncation, compare groups with log-rank and weighted tests, and compute restricted mean survival times.

statistics.name: Cox proportional hazards modelling
statistics.gist: Fit Cox models with time-varying covariates and stratification, test proportional hazards using Schoenfeld residuals, and report hazard ratios and adjusted survival curves.

statistics.name: Parametric and accelerated failure time models
statistics.gist: Fit Weibull, log-logistic and generalized gamma survival models with interval or right censoring, and compare them for extrapolating mean survival.

statistics.name: Competing risks and multistate models
statistics.gist: Estimate cumulative incidence functions, fit cause-specific and Fine-Gray models, and compute transition probabilities in illness-death or multistate processes.

statistics.name: Frailty and recurrent event models
statistics.gist: Analyse clustered or recurrent failure times with shared frailty, Andersen-Gill or gap-time models, and estimate the heterogeneity variance.

statistics.name: Reliability and degradation analysis
statistics.gist: Model component lifetimes and degradation paths from accelerated life tests or field returns, and estimate B10 lives, warranty costs and repairable-system intensities.

statistics.name: Sample size and power analysis
statistics.gist: Compute required sample sizes analytically or by simulation for complex designs (clustered, repeated measures, survival endpoints, noninferiority), and tabulate power curves.

statistics.name: Factorial and fractional factorial designs
statistics.gist: Construct two-level and mixed-level fractional factorials with specified resolution and aliasing, analyse the effects with ANOVA and half-normal plots, and identify active factors.

statistics.name: Response surface methodology
statistics.gist: Design central composite or Box-Behnken experiments, fit second-order models, and locate optimal operating conditions with canonical analysis or desirability functions.

statistics.name: Optimal experimental design
statistics.gist: Construct D-, A- or I-optimal designs for linear and nonlinear models with coordinate-exchange or multiplicative algorithms, and verify optimality with equivalence theorems.

statistics.name: Blocking, split-plot and Latin square designs
statistics.gist: Generate and analyse designs with restricted randomization, choosing the correct error strata and mixed-model ANOVA for whole-plot and sub-plot effects.

statistics.name: Group sequential and adaptive clinical trials
statistics.gist: Design trials with interim analyses using alpha-spending boundaries, simulate operating characteristics, and compute adjusted estimates and p-values at stopping.

statistics.name: Online A/B testing and experimentation
statistics.gist: Analyse randomized product experiments with variance reduction (CUPED), ratio metrics via the delta method, sample-ratio-mismatch checks and sequential testing.

statistics.name: Multi-armed bandits and adaptive allocation
statistics.gist: Simulate and evaluate Thompson sampling, UCB and response-adaptive randomization policies, computing regret and inference corrections for adaptively collected data.

statistics.name: Propensity score methods
statistics.gist: Estimate treatment effects from observational data by propensity matching, inverse probability weighting and overlap weights, and check covariate balance and positivity.

statistics.name: Doubly robust and machine learning causal estimation
statistics.gist: Implement AIPW, TMLE and double/debiased machine learning with cross-fitting to estimate average and conditional treatment effects with valid confidence intervals.

statistics.name: Difference-in-differences and event studies
statistics.gist: Estimate policy effects from panel data with two-way fixed effects and staggered-adoption estimators, test pre-trends, and report dynamic treatment effects.

statistics.name: Synthetic control methods
statistics.gist: Construct weighted donor-pool counterfactuals for single treated units, assess fit in the pre-treatment period, and run placebo-in-space and placebo-in-time inference.

statistics.name: Instrumental variables and regression discontinuity
statistics.gist: Estimate causal effects with two-stage least squares and weak-instrument diagnostics, or with local polynomial RD at a cutoff with bandwidth selection and density tests.

statistics.name: Causal discovery and graphical models
statistics.gist: Learn DAG or Markov equivalence structures from observational data with PC, GES or LiNGAM, estimate Gaussian graphical models with the graphical lasso, and identify adjustment sets.

statistics.name: Mediation and sensitivity analysis
statistics.gist: Decompose total effects into natural direct and indirect effects, and quantify robustness to unmeasured confounding with E-values or bias-parameter sweeps.

statistics.name: Missing data and multiple imputation
statistics.gist: Diagnose missingness mechanisms, perform chained-equation or model-based multiple imputation, pool estimates with Rubin's rules, and run MNAR sensitivity analyses.

statistics.name: Survey sampling and weighting
statistics.gist: Compute design-based estimates and variances under stratified cluster sampling, calibrate weights by raking, and use replicate-weight variance estimation.

statistics.name: Meta-analysis and evidence synthesis
statistics.gist: Pool effect sizes with fixed- and random-effects models, estimate heterogeneity, test for publication bias, and fit meta-regression or network meta-analysis.

statistics.name: Longitudinal and repeated-measures analysis
statistics.gist: Model within-subject trajectories with GEE under various working correlations or with growth-curve models, handling unbalanced visit times and dropout.

statistics.name: Spatial statistics and geostatistical kriging
statistics.gist: Estimate variograms, fit Gaussian random field models, krige to prediction grids with uncertainty, and test for spatial autocorrelation in areal data.

statistics.name: Spatial and temporal point processes
statistics.gist: Analyse event locations or times with intensity estimation, Ripley's K, and inhomogeneous Poisson or self-exciting Hawkes model fitting.

statistics.name: Extreme value analysis
statistics.gist: Fit GEV to block maxima or generalized Pareto to threshold exceedances, select thresholds, and estimate return levels with profile-likelihood intervals, including nonstationary covariates.

statistics.name: Copulas and multivariate dependence
statistics.gist: Fit Gaussian, t and Archimedean copulas to joint data with arbitrary margins, assess tail dependence, and simulate joint scenarios for risk estimates.

statistics.name: Latent variable and factor analysis
statistics.gist: Fit exploratory and confirmatory factor models or structural equation models, assess fit indices and measurement invariance, and compute factor scores.

statistics.name: Functional data analysis
statistics.gist: Represent curves or densely sampled trajectories with basis expansions, run functional PCA, fit functional regression and ANOVA, and register misaligned curves by time warping.

statistics.name: Compositional data analysis
statistics.gist: Analyse proportions that sum to a constant using additive, centred and isometric log-ratio transforms, handle structural and rounded zeros, and fit regression or PCA in the simplex.

statistics.name: Circular and directional statistics
statistics.gist: Summarize and model angles, times of day and orientations with von Mises and wrapped distributions, run Rayleigh and Watson tests, and fit circular-linear regressions.

statistics.name: Kernel density estimation and local polynomial smoothing
statistics.gist: Estimate univariate and multivariate densities and regression functions with kernel methods, select bandwidths by plug-in or cross-validation, and build variability bands.

statistics.name: Gaussian process regression
statistics.gist: Fit GP models with composite covariance kernels by marginal likelihood, use sparse or inducing-point approximations for larger data, and report predictive means and calibrated intervals.

statistics.name: Conformal prediction and distribution-free uncertainty
statistics.gist: Wrap arbitrary predictors with split, cross or jackknife+ conformal procedures to get finite-sample coverage, including conditional, weighted and time-series variants, and verify empirical coverage.

statistics.name: Cluster analysis and cluster validation
statistics.gist: Partition data with k-means, k-medoids, hierarchical and density-based algorithms, choose the number of clusters by silhouette, gap statistic or stability, and compare partitions with adjusted Rand indices.

statistics.name: Dimensionality reduction and matrix factorization
statistics.gist: Extract low-dimensional structure with PCA, robust PCA, ICA, NMF and multidimensional scaling, select rank by parallel analysis or cross-validation, and interpret loadings.

statistics.name: Tree ensembles and model interpretation
statistics.gist: Train random forests and gradient-boosted trees on tabular data, tune them with proper validation, and explain them with permutation importance, partial dependence, ALE and Shapley values.

statistics.name: Multivariate outlier and anomaly detection
statistics.gist: Flag anomalous observations using robust covariance (MCD) Mahalanobis distances, isolation forests and local outlier factors, and set thresholds with controlled false-alarm rates.

statistics.name: Statistical process control
statistics.gist: Build Shewhart, CUSUM, EWMA and multivariate Hotelling T-squared control charts, estimate phase I limits, compute average run lengths, and assess process capability indices.

statistics.name: Item response theory and psychometric scaling
statistics.gist: Fit Rasch, 2PL/3PL and graded response models to test or questionnaire responses, estimate abilities, assess item fit and differential item functioning, and equate test forms.

statistics.name: Paired comparison and ranking models
statistics.gist: Infer latent strengths from pairwise contests or ranked lists with Bradley-Terry, Thurstone, Plackett-Luce and Elo-type models, including ties, home advantage and uncertainty in rankings.

statistics.name: Capture-recapture and abundance estimation
statistics.gist: Estimate population size and survival from mark-recapture histories (Lincoln-Petersen, closed-population, Cormack-Jolly-Seber models) or from distance sampling detection functions.

statistics.name: Diagnostic test accuracy and ROC analysis
statistics.gist: Estimate sensitivity, specificity, predictive values and ROC/AUC with confidence intervals, compare correlated ROC curves, choose optimal cutpoints, and correct for verification bias or a missing gold standard via latent class models.

statistics.name: Method agreement and inter-rater reliability
statistics.gist: Quantify agreement between instruments or raters with Bland-Altman limits, Lin's concordance, Cohen's and Fleiss' kappa, weighted kappa and ICC variants, including repeated-measurement designs.

statistics.name: Hidden Markov models and regime switching
statistics.gist: Fit discrete-state HMMs and Markov-switching regressions by EM or direct likelihood, decode state sequences with Viterbi and forward-backward, and choose the number of states.

statistics.name: Sequential Monte Carlo and particle filtering
statistics.gist: Implement bootstrap and auxiliary particle filters and particle MCMC for nonlinear non-Gaussian state space models, with resampling schemes and estimation of likelihoods and parameters.

statistics.name: Approximate Bayesian computation and simulation-based inference
statistics.gist: Infer parameters of simulator models with intractable likelihoods using rejection and SMC-ABC, synthetic likelihood and summary-statistic selection, and validate posterior calibration.

statistics.name: Goodness-of-fit and two-sample distribution testing
statistics.gist: Fit candidate parametric distributions and test them with Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Anderson-Darling, Cramer-von Mises and chi-square tests, or compare samples with energy distance and kernel MMD tests.

statistics.name: Shape-constrained and isotonic regression
statistics.gist: Estimate monotone, convex or unimodal regression functions and densities by pool-adjacent-violators and constrained least squares, and test the shape restriction.

statistics.name: Small area estimation
statistics.gist: Produce reliable estimates for domains with tiny samples using Fay-Herriot area-level and nested-error unit-level models, empirical best predictors and MSE estimation.

statistics.name: Probabilistic record linkage
statistics.gist: Link records across files without unique identifiers using string-similarity comparisons, blocking and Fellegi-Sunter models fitted by EM, and estimate linkage error rates.

statistics.name: Statistical network analysis
statistics.gist: Model relational data with stochastic block models, latent space models and exponential random graph models, estimate community structure, and test network properties against null models.

statistics.name: Probabilistic forecast evaluation and combination
statistics.gist: Score density and quantile forecasts with proper scoring rules (CRPS, log score, pinball loss), assess calibration with PIT histograms, test predictive accuracy with Diebold-Mariano, and optimize forecast combinations.

statistics.name: Dynamic factor models and nowcasting
statistics.gist: Extract common factors from large panels of time series by principal components or state space EM, handle mixed frequencies and ragged edges, and nowcast low-frequency targets.

statistics.name: Panel data econometrics
statistics.gist: Estimate fixed- and random-effects panel models, choose between them with Hausman tests, use cluster-robust inference, and fit dynamic panels by Arellano-Bond or system GMM with instrument diagnostics.

statistics.name: Censored, truncated and sample-selection regression
statistics.gist: Fit Tobit, truncated regression and Heckman selection models for limited dependent variables by maximum likelihood or two-step estimation, and compute marginal effects.

statistics.name: Computer experiments and global sensitivity analysis
statistics.gist: Design space-filling (Latin hypercube, maximin) runs of expensive simulators, build emulators, and compute Sobol, Morris and variance-based sensitivity indices with uncertainty propagation.

statistics.name: Differential privacy and statistical disclosure control
statistics.gist: Release statistics and synthetic data under formal privacy guarantees with Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms and privacy accounting, or apply k-anonymity and cell suppression, and quantify the utility loss.

statistics.name: Latent class and latent profile analysis
statistics.gist: Fit finite mixture models with categorical or continuous indicators by EM to find unobserved subgroups. Choose the number of classes by BIC, entropy and the bootstrap likelihood-ratio test, then relate class membership to covariates with bias-adjusted three-step methods.

statistics.name: Generalized linear mixed models
statistics.gist: Fit binary, binomial and count outcomes with random effects using Laplace approximation, adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature or penalized quasi-likelihood. Compare conditional with marginal (population-averaged) effects and test variance components on the boundary.

statistics.name: Joint models for longitudinal and time-to-event data
statistics.gist: Link a mixed-effects trajectory of a repeatedly measured biomarker to a hazard model through shared random effects. Estimate the association parameters and produce dynamic, subject-specific survival predictions as new measurements arrive.

statistics.name: Distributed lag and environmental time-series regression
statistics.gist: Model delayed and nonlinear exposure-response effects of pollution or temperature on daily health counts with distributed lag (non)linear models in quasi-Poisson regression. Control for seasonality and trend, and report cumulative relative risks and attributable fractions.

statistics.name: Nonlinear mixed-effects and population pharmacokinetic modelling
statistics.gist: Fit compartmental or mechanistic models with between-subject random effects to sparse, irregular concentration-time data by FOCE-type or SAEM estimation. Assess covariate effects, residual error models and fit with visual predictive checks.

statistics.name: Monte Carlo integration and variance reduction
statistics.gist: Estimate expectations, tail probabilities and integrals by importance sampling, control variates, antithetic and stratified sampling or randomized quasi-Monte Carlo. Quantify Monte Carlo error and the effective sample size gains.

statistics.name: Bayesian variable selection and shrinkage priors
statistics.gist: Fit regressions with spike-and-slab, horseshoe or g-priors by MCMC or stochastic search. Compute posterior inclusion probabilities and median-probability models, and perform Bayesian model averaging of predictions.

statistics.name: Relative survival and cure models
statistics.gist: Estimate net and excess-hazard survival against population life tables using Ederer and Pohar-Perme estimators. Fit mixture or non-mixture cure models to estimate the cured fraction and the survival of the uncured.

statistics.name: Mortality modelling and life table construction
statistics.gist: Build period and cohort life tables from deaths and exposures, graduate mortality rates with parametric laws (Gompertz, Heligman-Pollard) or smoothing, and forecast mortality with Lee-Carter or Cairns-Blake-Dowd models.

statistics.name: Age-period-cohort analysis
statistics.gist: Decompose rates tabulated by age and calendar time into age, period and cohort effects with Poisson APC models. Handle the identification problem through estimable functions, drift and curvature parameters, and project future rates.

statistics.name: Matched case-control and conditional logistic regression
statistics.gist: Analyse individually matched or stratified case-control and case-crossover data with conditional likelihood. Estimate odds ratios with interactions, and compare them against unconditional and Mantel-Haenszel estimates under sparse strata.

statistics.name: Bayesian disease mapping and areal models
statistics.gist: Smooth standardized incidence or mortality ratios across small areas with conditional autoregressive, BYM and Leroux priors. Compute the posterior exceedance probabilities of the relative risks and detect high-risk clusters.

statistics.name: Reproduction number estimation and epidemic nowcasting
statistics.gist: Estimate time-varying reproduction numbers from incidence curves with renewal-equation methods and serial-interval distributions. Correct recent counts for reporting delays and right truncation, and quantify the uncertainty in the trajectories.

statistics.name: Multivariate linear models, MANOVA and canonical correlation
statistics.gist: Test hypotheses on several correlated responses with Wilks, Pillai and Hotelling-Lawley statistics and profile analysis. Fit reduced-rank and multivariate regressions, and extract canonical correlations and variates with significance tests.

statistics.name: ANOVA contrasts and simultaneous multiple comparisons
statistics.gist: Analyse unbalanced one- and multi-way layouts with type II/III sums of squares, planned contrasts and estimated marginal means. Report Tukey, Dunnett, Scheffe and step-down simultaneous intervals with family-wise error control.

statistics.name: Crossover designs and bioequivalence
statistics.gist: Analyse two-period and higher-order crossover trials with period, sequence and carryover effects. Establish average or scaled bioequivalence from log-transformed pharmacokinetic metrics using two one-sided tests and 90% confidence intervals.

statistics.name: Phase I dose-finding designs
statistics.gist: Simulate and compare dose-escalation designs (3+3, continual reassessment method, BOIN, escalation with overdose control) for locating a maximum tolerated dose. Tabulate the operating characteristics: the probability of correct selection, the allocation and the toxicity rates.

statistics.name: Exponential smoothing and time series decomposition
statistics.gist: Fit ETS models with additive or multiplicative error, trend and seasonality, and decompose series with STL or classical seasonal adjustment. Handle multiple seasonalities and produce forecasts with model-based prediction intervals.

statistics.name: Nonlinear and threshold time series models
statistics.gist: Test for nonlinearity and fit threshold (TAR, SETAR), smooth-transition and bilinear autoregressions. Estimate the thresholds by grid search with nonstandard inference, and compare their forecasts with linear benchmarks.

statistics.name: Occupancy and imperfect detection models
statistics.gist: Estimate site occupancy and detection probabilities from repeated presence-absence surveys with single-season, multi-season and N-mixture models. Fit the effects of site and survey covariates, and assess goodness-of-fit.

statistics.name: Species richness and diversity estimation
statistics.gist: Estimate the number of unseen species and Hill-number diversity profiles from abundance or incidence samples using Chao, ACE and coverage-based rarefaction and extrapolation. Report bootstrap confidence intervals and compare communities.

statistics.name: Insurance claims reserving and credibility
statistics.gist: Project outstanding liabilities from run-off triangles with chain ladder, Mack, Bornhuetter-Ferguson and bootstrap ODP models. Compute Buhlmann and Buhlmann-Straub credibility premiums for heterogeneous portfolios.

statistics.name: Beta and fractional response regression
statistics.gist: Model continuous outcomes bounded in (0,1), such as rates and proportions, with beta, zero-one-inflated beta and quasi-likelihood fractional logit regressions. Allow covariate-dependent precision and report average marginal effects.

statistics.name: Gamma, inverse Gaussian and Tweedie GLMs
statistics.gist: Model positive skewed continuous outcomes and semicontinuous data with exact zeros using gamma, inverse Gaussian and compound Poisson-gamma Tweedie GLMs. Estimate the power and dispersion parameters, choose the link function, and compare against log-normal models.

statistics.name: Distributional regression and reference centile curves
statistics.gist: Model the location, scale and shape of a response distribution as smooth covariate functions with GAMLSS or LMS methods. Construct age-specific reference centiles and z-scores, and check them with worm plots and Q-statistics.

statistics.name: G-methods for time-varying treatments
statistics.gist: Estimate the effects of sustained or dynamic treatment strategies under time-varying confounding with marginal structural models fitted by stabilized inverse probability weights, the parametric g-formula and g-estimation of structural nested models. Frame the analysis as target-trial emulation.

statistics.name: Exact and small-sample inference for proportions and rates
statistics.gist: Compute and compare Clopper-Pearson, Wilson, Jeffreys and mid-p intervals for binomial and Poisson parameters. Build intervals for differences and ratios of proportions and rates, and evaluate their actual coverage at small counts.

statistics.name: Simulation studies of statistical methods
statistics.gist: Design and run Monte Carlo experiments that compare estimators or tests on bias, empirical standard error, coverage, power and type I error. Report Monte Carlo standard errors and use factorial scenario designs.

statistics.name: Mendelian randomization with summary statistics
statistics.gist: Estimate causal effects from genetic-variant association summaries with inverse-variance weighted, MR-Egger, weighted median and mode estimators. Assess heterogeneity, pleiotropy and weak-instrument bias, and run leave-one-out sensitivity analyses.

statistics.name: Analytical calibration, inverse prediction and nondetects
statistics.gist: Fit calibration curves with weighted or heteroscedastic regression and invert them to estimate unknown concentrations with confidence intervals. Compute detection and quantification limits, and analyse left-censored measurements below the limits with ROS or censored maximum likelihood.

operations-research.name: Mixed-integer facility location
operations-research.gist: Choose sites to open and assign demand points under capacity and fixed costs; formulate and solve capacitated or uncapacitated location MILPs and report optimal sites, flows and cost.

operations-research.name: Capacitated vehicle routing with time windows
operations-research.gist: Plan delivery routes for a fleet with vehicle capacities and customer time windows; build distance matrices from coordinates, solve with OR-Tools or heuristics, and report routes and total distance.

operations-research.name: Pickup-and-delivery and dial-a-ride routing
operations-research.gist: Route vehicles that must pair pickups with drop-offs under precedence, ride-time and capacity limits; compute feasible schedules and minimize cost or passenger inconvenience.

operations-research.name: Arc routing for street services
operations-research.gist: Cover required street segments for snow plowing, waste collection or meter reading; solve Chinese-postman and capacitated arc routing variants on road graphs.

operations-research.name: Job-shop and flow-shop scheduling
operations-research.gist: Sequence operations of jobs on machines to minimize makespan or tardiness; model with constraint programming or disjunctive MILPs and verify schedule feasibility.

operations-research.name: Parallel-machine scheduling with setups
operations-research.gist: Assign and sequence jobs on identical or unrelated machines with sequence-dependent setup times; compare dispatching rules, local search and exact formulations.

operations-research.name: Resource-constrained project scheduling
operations-research.gist: Schedule project activities with precedence relations and renewable resource limits; compute critical paths, resource profiles and makespan-minimizing schedules.

operations-research.name: Nurse and workforce rostering
operations-research.gist: Build shift rosters satisfying coverage demand, labor rules and staff preferences; solve with CP-SAT or integer programming and report violations and fairness metrics.

operations-research.name: Crew pairing and airline crew scheduling
operations-research.gist: Generate legal duty pairings from flight legs and select a minimum-cost covering set; implement set partitioning with column generation or heuristics.

operations-research.name: Timetabling for schools and exams
operations-research.gist: Assign courses or exams to rooms and time slots avoiding conflicts and capacity overflows; formulate graph-coloring-style constraints and minimize soft-constraint penalties.

operations-research.name: Public transport service planning
operations-research.gist: Plan public transport services such as rail, bus, metro and ferry. Work includes line planning and frequency setting, stop and station placement, timetable synchronization, platform and track allocation, passenger route choice and demand assignment, fare and capacity planning, and delay propagation analysis. Methods include integer programming, network models, heuristics and simulation, evaluated on operator and passenger cost metrics.

operations-research.name: Vehicle and fleet scheduling in transit
operations-research.gist: Assign vehicles to timetabled trips minimizing fleet size and deadheading; solve single- and multi-depot vehicle scheduling as network-flow or set-cover problems.

operations-research.name: Queueing network performance analysis
operations-research.gist: Model service systems as Jackson or closed product-form networks; compute throughputs, utilizations and waiting times via mean-value analysis and validate against simulation.

operations-research.name: Call-center staffing with Erlang models
operations-research.gist: Determine agent levels across intervals to meet service-level targets using Erlang C/A models with abandonment, and fit arrival-rate forecasts from call logs.

operations-research.name: Discrete-event simulation of service systems
operations-research.gist: Build event-driven simulations of clinics, ports or warehouses with stochastic arrivals and service; estimate performance measures with confidence intervals and warm-up removal.

operations-research.name: Simulation output analysis and variance reduction
operations-research.gist: Analyze stochastic simulation outputs with batch means, replications, common random numbers and control variates to obtain efficient, valid estimates.

operations-research.name: Single-echelon inventory control policies
operations-research.gist: Optimize (s,S), (r,Q) or base-stock policies under stochastic demand and lead times; compute costs and fill rates analytically or by simulation from demand histories.

operations-research.name: Multi-echelon inventory optimization
operations-research.gist: Set safety stocks and base-stock levels across serial or distribution networks using guaranteed-service or stochastic-service models, including repairable spare parts with METRIC/VARI-METRIC approximations and marginal-analysis allocation, and evaluate system cost, backorders or availability.

operations-research.name: Perishable and newsvendor inventory problems
operations-research.gist: Choose order quantities for perishable or single-period goods from demand data, including censored-demand estimation, quantile solutions and multi-product budget constraints.

operations-research.name: Lot sizing and production planning
operations-research.gist: Plan production quantities over time with setup costs and capacities; solve Wagner-Whitin, capacitated multi-item lot sizing MILPs and rolling-horizon plans.

operations-research.name: Material requirements and aggregate planning
operations-research.gist: Derive time-phased component requirements from bills of materials and master schedules, and optimize aggregate workforce, overtime and inventory plans with LP.

operations-research.name: Demand forecasting for operations planning
operations-research.gist: Forecast intermittent or seasonal item demand with Croston, exponential smoothing or ARIMA methods and evaluate forecast accuracy in terms of downstream inventory cost.

operations-research.name: Two-stage stochastic programming
operations-research.gist: Formulate recourse models for capacity or planning decisions under scenario uncertainty; solve extensive forms or L-shaped decomposition and report VSS and EVPI.

operations-research.name: Scenario generation and reduction
operations-research.gist: Build scenario trees from historical or simulated uncertainty via moment matching, clustering or Wasserstein-based reduction and assess solution stability.

operations-research.name: Multistage stochastic optimization and SDDP
operations-research.gist: Solve multistage planning problems such as reservoir or inventory operation with stochastic dual dynamic programming or nested decomposition and evaluate policies out of sample.

operations-research.name: Chance-constrained optimization
operations-research.gist: Enforce probabilistic constraints in planning via sample average approximation, scenario approach or convex approximations and verify empirical violation rates.

operations-research.name: Robust and distributionally robust optimization
operations-research.gist: Protect decisions against uncertainty sets or ambiguity sets of distributions; derive tractable reformulations in cvxpy and compare against nominal solutions.

operations-research.name: Sample average approximation and statistical bounds
operations-research.gist: Solve stochastic programs by sampling, and compute optimality-gap confidence intervals with multiple replications procedures.

operations-research.name: Markov decision processes for operations
operations-research.gist: Model sequential decisions in maintenance, admission control or replenishment as MDPs; solve by value or policy iteration and characterize threshold structure.

operations-research.name: Approximate dynamic programming
operations-research.gist: Approximate value functions for large-state resource allocation problems using basis-function regression or rollout and benchmark against myopic and exact policies.

operations-research.name: Maintenance and replacement optimization
operations-research.gist: Fit failure-time distributions from equipment data and optimize preventive maintenance intervals, inspection schedules or replacement policies minimizing long-run cost.

operations-research.name: Minimum-cost network flow modeling
operations-research.gist: Model transshipment, distribution or assignment problems as min-cost flows; solve with network simplex or LP and interpret duals as node potentials.

operations-research.name: Multicommodity flow and network design
operations-research.gist: Route multiple commodities over capacitated networks and choose which arcs to install; solve fixed-charge network design with MILP, Benders or relaxations.

operations-research.name: Maximum flow and minimum cut analysis
operations-research.gist: Compute max flows, min cuts and network reliability or vulnerability measures on infrastructure graphs, including interdiction of critical arcs.

operations-research.name: Shortest paths and resource-constrained paths
operations-research.gist: Compute shortest, k-shortest or resource-constrained shortest paths on large road or transit graphs, including time-dependent travel times and labeling algorithms.

operations-research.name: Traffic assignment and equilibrium
operations-research.gist: Compute user-equilibrium and system-optimal flows on road networks with BPR link costs using Frank-Wolfe or path-based algorithms and evaluate Braess-type effects.

operations-research.name: Supply chain network design
operations-research.gist: Optimize plant, warehouse and lane decisions across multi-echelon supply chains with capacity, service and transport cost tradeoffs, including scenario sensitivity.

operations-research.name: Column generation and branch-and-price
operations-research.gist: Solve large set-partitioning models such as cutting or covering by pricing subproblems, track LP bounds and recover integer solutions.

operations-research.name: Cutting stock and bin packing
operations-research.gist: Minimize raw-material waste when cutting rolls or sheets, or pack items into bins and containers, using pattern-based LPs and packing heuristics.

operations-research.name: Lagrangian relaxation and decomposition bounds
operations-research.gist: Relax complicating constraints of hard integer programs, optimize multipliers by subgradient or bundle methods, and compute bounds and primal heuristics.

operations-research.name: Benders decomposition implementations
operations-research.gist: Decompose mixed-integer models into master and subproblems, generate optimality and feasibility cuts, and track convergence of bounds.

operations-research.name: Cutting planes and MILP formulation strength
operations-research.gist: Compare alternative MILP formulations, add valid inequalities and measure LP-relaxation gaps and solver performance on generated instances.

operations-research.name: Metaheuristics for combinatorial optimization
operations-research.gist: Design simulated annealing, tabu search, genetic or large-neighborhood search for hard combinatorial problems and statistically compare their solution quality.

operations-research.name: Quadratic assignment and layout problems
operations-research.gist: Assign facilities to locations or design plant layouts minimizing flow-distance cost with QAP formulations, local search and lower bounds.

operations-research.name: Assignment and matching markets
operations-research.gist: Solve linear, bottleneck and generalized assignment problems and stable-matching variants for allocating workers, students or organs, verifying optimality or stability.

operations-research.name: Revenue management and dynamic pricing
operations-research.gist: Set booking limits, bid prices or dynamic prices for perishable capacity using EMSR heuristics, network LPs and demand models estimated from sales data.

operations-research.name: Healthcare operations and appointment scheduling
operations-research.gist: Schedule outpatient appointments, operating rooms or beds under no-shows and stochastic durations, balancing waiting, idle time and overtime.

operations-research.name: Warehouse operations and order picking
operations-research.gist: Optimize slotting, picker routing and batching in warehouses using layout-based distance models and simulation of order streams.

operations-research.name: Energy system unit commitment and dispatch
operations-research.gist: Schedule generators with startup costs, ramping and reserve constraints over time horizons via MILP, and compute economic dispatch and locational prices.

operations-research.name: Emergency service location and dispatch
operations-research.gist: Site ambulances or fire stations with coverage models such as MCLP or hypercube queueing and evaluate response-time distributions.

operations-research.name: Portfolio and capital budgeting optimization
operations-research.gist: Select projects or assets under budget and risk constraints with mean-variance, CVaR or integer knapsack-type models and compute efficient frontiers.

operations-research.name: Multi-objective optimization and Pareto fronts
operations-research.gist: Compute Pareto-optimal tradeoffs in planning problems with epsilon-constraint or weighted-sum methods and evaluate front quality indicators.

operations-research.name: Sensitivity analysis and LP duality
operations-research.gist: Extract shadow prices, reduced costs and ranging information from LP solutions and verify parametric behavior as data change.

operations-research.name: Data envelopment analysis efficiency
operations-research.gist: Measure relative efficiency of decision-making units like hospitals or branches with CCR/BCC DEA LPs, slacks and Malmquist productivity indices.

operations-research.name: Nonlinear and convex resource allocation
operations-research.gist: Solve continuous allocation problems with concave returns or convex costs using KKT conditions, convex solvers and verification of optimality conditions.

operations-research.name: Online and rolling-horizon decision policies
operations-research.gist: Evaluate online algorithms and rolling-horizon reoptimization for dynamic arrivals of orders or requests against offline optimal benchmarks by simulation.

operations-research.name: Container terminal and port logistics
operations-research.gist: Optimize berth allocation, quay crane assignment and yard stacking for container terminals with MILP and simulation of vessel arrivals.

operations-research.name: Inventory routing and replenishment logistics
operations-research.gist: Jointly decide delivery quantities and routes for vendor-managed customers over a horizon, balancing holding, stockout and transport costs.

operations-research.name: Queueing model estimation from event logs
operations-research.gist: Infer arrival processes, service-time distributions and queue parameters from timestamped event data, test model fit and predict delays.

operations-research.name: Combinatorial auctions and procurement optimization
operations-research.gist: Solve winner determination and supplier selection problems with bundle bids, quantity discounts and capacity constraints via integer programming.

operations-research.name: Traveling salesman problems and variants
operations-research.gist: Solve symmetric, asymmetric and constrained TSP variants from coordinates or distance matrices with subtour-elimination MILPs, Held-Karp bounds, 2-opt/Or-opt/Lin-Kernighan heuristics, and report tours and optimality gaps.

operations-research.name: Orienteering and prize-collecting routing
operations-research.gist: Select and sequence a profitable subset of locations under time or distance budgets, including team orienteering and prize-collecting TSP variants, solved with MILP, labeling or local search.

operations-research.name: Electric vehicle and drone routing
operations-research.gist: Route battery-limited vehicles or truck-drone tandems with charging stops, energy consumption models and recharge times; build feasible routes and compare against conventional routing baselines.

operations-research.name: Hub location and hub-and-spoke network design
operations-research.gist: Locate hubs and allocate origin-destination flows with inter-hub discount factors under single or multiple allocation; solve p-hub median and capacitated hub MILPs on air or postal flow data.

operations-research.name: Continuous and planar location problems
operations-research.gist: Find optimal facility coordinates in the plane under minisum (Weber), minimax or obnoxious objectives using Weiszfeld iterations, convex solvers and geometric algorithms, and verify optimality conditions.

operations-research.name: Districting and territory design
operations-research.gist: Partition geographic units into balanced, contiguous and compact districts for sales, service or political zoning; use MILP with contiguity constraints, graph partitioning or local search, and report compactness and balance metrics.

operations-research.name: Steiner trees and survivable network design
operations-research.gist: Connect terminal nodes at minimum cost with Steiner trees, degree- or hop-constrained spanning trees, or k-edge-connected topologies; use cut-based formulations, approximations and reliability checks.

operations-research.name: Dynamic network flows and evacuation planning
operations-research.gist: Model time-varying movement through capacitated networks with time-expanded graphs; compute quickest flows, earliest-arrival flows and evacuation clearance times for buildings or regions.

operations-research.name: Airline fleet assignment and aircraft routing
operations-research.gist: Assign aircraft types to flight legs on time-space networks and build maintenance-feasible tail routings; solve multicommodity flow MILPs and evaluate spill and operating costs.

operations-research.name: Runway and aircraft landing scheduling
operations-research.gist: Sequence aircraft landings and takeoffs with time windows and wake-separation requirements; solve with MILP, dynamic programming or constrained position shifting, and measure delay and throughput.

operations-research.name: Maritime ship routing and scheduling
operations-research.gist: Plan liner or tramp shipping routes, speeds and cargo selection with port time windows and fuel-speed curves; optimize fleet deployment and bunkering costs with MILP or set partitioning.

operations-research.name: Bike-sharing and car-sharing rebalancing
operations-research.gist: Estimate station demand imbalances from trip data and plan repositioning vehicle routes and target inventories, using static or dynamic rebalancing models and simulation of service levels.

operations-research.name: Humanitarian and disaster relief logistics
operations-research.gist: Preposition relief supplies and plan last-mile distribution under damaged networks and uncertain needs, using equity-aware objectives, scenario-based models and deprivation-cost functions.

operations-research.name: Assembly line balancing
operations-research.gist: Assign tasks with precedence relations to workstations to minimize stations or cycle time (SALBP-1/2), including mixed-model and U-shaped lines, via MILP, branch-and-bound and priority heuristics.

operations-research.name: Production line throughput and buffer allocation
operations-research.gist: Evaluate serial and assembly lines with unreliable machines and finite buffers using decomposition approximations or Markov models, and optimize buffer sizes for throughput targets.

operations-research.name: Sports league scheduling
operations-research.gist: Construct round-robin tournament schedules minimizing breaks or travel distance under venue and fairness constraints, using circle-method constructions, CP-SAT and the traveling tournament problem.

operations-research.name: Open-pit mine planning
operations-research.gist: Compute ultimate pit limits from block models via max-flow/Lerchs-Grossmann, and schedule block extraction over periods with precedence and capacity constraints to maximize net present value.

operations-research.name: Blending and pooling problems
operations-research.gist: Optimize mixing of raw materials into products meeting quality specifications, from linear diet and feed blending to nonconvex bilinear pooling models solved with McCormick relaxations or local NLP.

operations-research.name: Simulation optimization and ranking-and-selection
operations-research.gist: Select the best system design among simulated alternatives with indifference-zone, OCBA or Bayesian procedures, or tune continuous parameters with stochastic approximation and gradient estimators.

operations-research.name: Matrix-analytic methods and phase-type queues
operations-research.gist: Analyze quasi-birth-death processes and M/PH/1, MAP/PH/c queues by computing rate matrices, stationary distributions and delay moments, and fit phase-type distributions to service data.

operations-research.name: Priority, polling and M/G/1-type queues
operations-research.gist: Derive and compute waiting times under preemptive and non-preemptive priorities, vacations, polling disciplines and the c-mu rule using Pollaczek-Khinchine and conservation laws, and check them against simulation.

operations-research.name: Fluid and heavy-traffic approximations
operations-research.gist: Approximate congested queueing and manufacturing systems with fluid models, diffusion limits and Halfin-Whitt scaling; compare approximation accuracy against exact results or simulation.

operations-research.name: Multi-armed bandits and Gittins index policies
operations-research.gist: Solve stochastic scheduling and sequential allocation problems with Gittins or Whittle indices, and evaluate bandit learning policies (UCB, Thompson sampling) by regret in operational settings.

operations-research.name: Bilevel optimization and Stackelberg models
operations-research.gist: Model leader-follower decisions such as toll setting, pricing or interdiction; reformulate with KKT or strong-duality conditions into single-level MILPs and solve or bound them.

operations-research.name: Inverse optimization

applied-mathematics.gist: Fitting nonlinear parametric models to data with Gauss-Newton, Levenberg-Marquardt or variable projection for separable problems, handling poor starting values and parameter correlations, and reporting covariance-based uncertainties.

applied-mathematics.name: Rare-event simulation and importance sampling
applied-mathematics.gist: Estimating very small probabilities and tail quantities with importance sampling, cross-entropy methods, subset simulation or splitting, and comparing relative error and cost against crude Monte Carlo.

applied-mathematics.name: Stochastic simulation of jump processes
applied-mathematics.gist: Simulating continuous-time Markov jump processes such as chemical reaction networks with Gillespie's algorithm, next-reaction or tau-leaping methods, and comparing moments and distributions with chemical-master-equation or diffusion approximations.

applied-mathematics.name: Numerical analysis of Markov chains
applied-mathematics.gist: Computing stationary distributions, mean first-passage times, committors, absorption probabilities and mixing rates of large discrete- or continuous-time Markov chains with sparse linear algebra and aggregation methods.

applied-mathematics.name: Graph signal processing
applied-mathematics.gist: Defining graph Fourier transforms, spectral and polynomial graph filters, graph wavelets and sampling or interpolation of signals on irregular networks and meshes, with Chebyshev approximations of Laplacian filters.

applied-mathematics.name: Nonlinear Kalman filtering and smoothing
applied-mathematics.gist: Estimating hidden states of nonlinear state-space models with extended, unscented or cubature Kalman filters and Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoothers, checking filter consistency through innovation statistics and NEES.

applied-mathematics.name: Feedback controller design and robust stability
applied-mathematics.gist: Designing PID, pole-placement, LQR/LQG or loop-shaping controllers for linear plants and verifying them with root locus, Bode/Nyquist margins, sensitivity functions and robustness to model uncertainty.

applied-mathematics.name: Sum-of-squares and LMI stability certificates
applied-mathematics.gist: Constructing Lyapunov functions, invariant sets and region-of-attraction estimates for polynomial or linear uncertain systems via semidefinite programming with linear matrix inequalities and sum-of-squares relaxations.

applied-mathematics.name: Compartmental model analysis
applied-mathematics.gist: Analysing epidemic, pharmacokinetic or ecological compartment ODE models through equilibria, next-generation-matrix reproduction numbers, final-size relations and threshold behaviour, checked against simulation.

applied-mathematics.name: Cellular automata and coupled map lattices
applied-mathematics.gist: Simulating discrete-space, discrete-time dynamics such as elementary and totalistic cellular automata or coupled logistic-map lattices, classifying their behaviour and measuring spatiotemporal entropy, defect statistics and correlation lengths.

applied-mathematics.name: Slow-fast systems and canards
applied-mathematics.gist: Analysing multiple-timescale ODEs with geometric singular perturbation theory, computing critical manifolds, relaxation oscillations, canard explosions and mixed-mode oscillations, and comparing reduced and full dynamics.

applied-mathematics.name: Lagrangian particle methods
applied-mathematics.gist: Solving continuum problems with smoothed particle hydrodynamics, vortex-blob or particle-in-cell methods, studying kernel choice, particle regularization and remeshing, and checking consistency and conservation.

applied-mathematics.name: Projection methods for incompressible flow
